prs.author: Crypt-iQ
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new fuzzing harness specifically designed to test Bitcoin Core's compact block message processing logic. This helps identify vulnerabilities or bugs in the compact block implementation, significantly enhancing the network's resilience and security against malformed block propagation.
prs.technical_summary: A dedicated fuzzing target is added to Bitcoin Core's existing fuzzing framework, focusing on the `CompactBlock` serialization and deserialization routines. The harness continuously feeds randomly generated or malformed compact block data to these functions, triggering edge cases that might lead to crashes, memory errors, or unexpected behavior. This proactive security testing improves the robustness of the P2P layer's block relay mechanism against potential Denial-of-Service attacks or protocol deviations.

prs.description: build: Add a compiler minimum feature check
prs.author: polespinasa
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a check during the build process to ensure that the compiler being used meets a minimum feature set requirement. This prevents compilation failures with outdated compilers and ensures the built software is compatible with modern C++ standards.
prs.technical_summary: The build system configuration (e.g., in `configure.ac` or `CMakeLists.txt`) is augmented with a series of compiler probes. These probes test for the presence of specific C++ language features (e.g., C++17 or C++20 standard library features) or verify a minimum compiler version. If the compiler does not satisfy these requirements, the build process will terminate early with an informative error, preventing obscure compilation errors and ensuring a consistent development environment.

prs.description: kernel: build: remove unused serfloat dependency
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR removes the unused `serfloat` dependency from the Bitcoin Core Kernel build system, streamlining the build process and reducing unnecessary complexity. This is a clean-up effort for the ongoing kernel development.
prs.technical_summary: The build system configuration for the Bitcoin Core Kernel is updated to no longer link against or include headers from the `serfloat` library. Investigations revealed that the `serfloat` functionality was either not utilized by the `btck` components or its functionality was replaced/inlined elsewhere. Removing this dependency simplifies compilation flags, reduces potential linking issues, and ensures a leaner build artifact for the kernel, improving maintainability.

prs.description: wallet: Enforce BDB btree levels and overflow item sizes
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR improves wallet database robustness by enforcing specific Berkeley DB (BDB) btree levels and overflow item sizes. This helps prevent database corruption and ensures more stable wallet operation.
prs.technical_summary: This change introduces explicit configuration for Berkeley DB's Btree levels and overflow page sizes within the wallet's database environment. By setting `DB_MAX_BTREE_PAGES` and `DB_MAX_TXN_PAGES`, it prevents potential issues arising from excessively deep Btrees or over-fragmented overflow pages, which can lead to performance degradation or corruption. This ensures more predictable and stable on-disk storage characteristics for wallet data, particularly for large wallets or those experiencing many transactions.

prs.description: CI: Add Riscv bare metal job
prs.author: sedited
prs.public_summary: This PR extends the Continuous Integration (CI) system by adding a job to build and test Bitcoin Core on Riscv bare metal. This ensures compatibility and proper functioning of the software on the emerging Riscv architecture.
prs.technical_summary: The CI pipeline automates building and testing across diverse platforms. This PR integrates a new CI job that compiles Bitcoin Core for the Riscv architecture and executes a suite of tests directly on bare metal (without an intervening operating system). This proactive testing verifies that the codebase correctly targets and performs on Riscv, enabling early detection of any architecture-specific bugs or incompatibilities.

prs.description: util: shorten thread names to avoid Linux truncation
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR shortens internal thread names to prevent truncation on Linux systems, improving debuggability and log readability. This makes it easier for developers and users to identify specific threads when inspecting system processes.
prs.technical_summary: The modification adjusts the string constants used for setting thread names in various parts of the codebase. On Linux, thread names are truncated to 15 characters; longer names appear incomplete in tools like `htop` or `/proc/pid/task/tid/comm`. Shortening these names ensures they are fully visible, making it easier to diagnose issues.

prs.description: BIP 434 Support: Peer feature negotiation
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR implements support for BIP 434, enabling peers to negotiate specific features during connection establishment. This adds value by laying the groundwork for future protocol upgrades and more flexible network interactions without requiring full network adoption simultaneously.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a `feature_bits` field to the P2P version message, allowing nodes to advertise their supported capabilities. The implementation involves modifying the P2P handshake protocol to process these new feature bits, enabling subsequent behavior adaptation based on the negotiated features. This enhancement likely extends `CNode` functionality to manage and react to various feature flags, ensuring backward compatibility while facilitating forward-looking protocol evolution.

prs.description: wallet: document importdescriptors error object fields
prs.author: satsfy
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the documentation for the `importdescriptors` RPC command by detailing the fields within its error object. This makes it easier for developers to understand and troubleshoot issues when programmatically importing wallet descriptors.
prs.technical_summary: This change updates the RPC help and schema documentation for the `importdescriptors` command. It explicitly lists and describes the structure and meaning of the fields within the error object returned by this RPC call, such as `success`, `error`, `descriptor`, `timestamp`, and `warnings`. This improved documentation allows external client applications to parse error responses more robustly and react appropriately to specific failure conditions during descriptor imports, enhancing API reliability.

prs.description: wallet: `addhdkey` RPC to add just keys to wallets via new `unused(KEY)` descriptor
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new RPC command, `addhdkey`, enabling users to add individual Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) keys to their wallets using a novel `unused(KEY)` descriptor format. This offers more granular control over key management without needing to import full descriptor templates.
prs.technical_summary: This PR implements the `addhdkey` RPC, which facilitates the direct addition of single HD public keys or master public keys to a wallet using a newly introduced `unused(KEY)` descriptor type. This descriptor internally wraps a given HD key, allowing the wallet to derive and track addresses from it for incoming funds. Unlike standard descriptors (e.g., `wpkh(key/0/*)`), `unused(KEY)` is designed for watch-only purposes and doesn't manage change outputs or full derivation paths, providing a lightweight way to monitor specific key chains without full wallet integration.

prs.description: validation: Explicitly move blocks to validation signals
prs.author: sedited
prs.public_summary: This PR modifies block validation to explicitly move blocks when signaling their validation status. This improves efficiency by avoiding unnecessary copies of large block objects.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, blocks passed to validation signals could involve expensive copy operations due to their size. This change updates the signaling mechanism to utilize `std::move` when dispatching blocks. By transferring ownership of the `CBlock` object to the signal handler, it eliminates the need for deep copies, significantly reducing memory overhead and improving performance within the block validation subsystem during processing and propagation.

prs.description: wallet: move fAbortRescan reset into WalletRescanReserver reserve function
prs.author: polespinasa
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors wallet rescan logic to ensure an 'abort rescan' flag is reliably reset at the correct time. This enhances the reliability and state management of wallet rescans, preventing stale flags from affecting future operations.
prs.technical_summary: The `fAbortRescan` flag is used to signal the termination of an ongoing wallet rescan. This change moves the logic responsible for resetting this flag (setting it to `false`) into the `WalletRescanReserver::reserve` function. This ensures that whenever a new rescan reservation is initiated, the `fAbortRescan` flag is always in a clean, false state, preventing a previous aborted state from incorrectly interfering with subsequent rescan attempts and improving the encapsulation of rescan state management.

prs.description: cli: Replace libevent usage with simple http client
prs.author: fjahr
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the `bitcoin-cli` tool to use a simpler, internal HTTP client instead of the external `libevent` library. This reduces an external dependency and simplifies the CLI's codebase.
prs.technical_summary: The `libevent` framework, previously utilized for HTTP client operations within `bitcoin-cli`, is replaced with a custom or more lightweight HTTP client implementation. This involves re-implementing HTTP request/response handling, connection management, and parsing within the CLI's internal code, thereby reducing the external footprint and complexity associated with `libevent` integration.

prs.description: coinselection: Optimize BnB exploration
prs.author: murchandamus
prs.public_summary: This PR significantly optimizes the Branch and Bound (BnB) coin selection algorithm, leading to faster transaction creation and potentially better fee utilization. It enhances the efficiency of finding optimal UTXO combinations for spending.
prs.technical_summary: The optimization focuses on refining the exploration strategy within the Branch and Bound algorithm. This involves introducing improved pruning techniques to discard unpromising branches earlier in the search tree, leveraging more efficient sorting or indexing of UTXOs, and potentially implementing enhanced heuristics to guide the search towards optimal solutions more quickly. The goal is to reduce the computational complexity and execution time required to identify a near-optimal or optimal set of UTXOs for a given transaction amount.

prs.description: contrib: Add bash completion for new bitcoin command
prs.author: caesrcd
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the `bitcoin` command-line experience by adding bash completion, making it easier and quicker for users to type commands and arguments. It improves usability by suggesting commands as they are typed.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a bash completion script to the `contrib/` directory. It parses the help output of the `bitcoin-cli` command to dynamically generate completion suggestions for the `bitcoin` command, covering subcommands, flags, and arguments. This leverages existing RPC descriptions to provide a rich completion experience without hardcoding the command structure.

prs.description: refactor: Change CChain methods to use references, add tests
prs.author: optout21
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors `CChain` methods to consistently use references instead of pointers, improving code safety and clarity. It also adds new tests to ensure the correctness of these changes.
prs.technical_summary: The PR modifies various methods of the `CChain` class, which manages the active blockchain, to accept and return `const CBlockIndex&` references instead of raw `CBlockIndex*` pointers. This design choice leverages C++'s reference semantics to guarantee that the objects exist and are not null, reducing potential dereferencing errors and improving type safety. New unit tests are introduced to validate the correct behavior of the updated methods, ensuring their robustness.

prs.description: wallet: Fix for duplicate external signers case
prs.author: optout21
prs.public_summary: This fix resolves an issue where external signers, such as hardware wallets, could be duplicated within the Bitcoin Core wallet system. This improves stability and reliability for users employing hardware wallets or other external signing devices.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a bug where the wallet's internal management of external signers (e.g., those interacting via HWI or PSBTs) could incorrectly register or represent the same external signer multiple times. The solution likely involves refining the identification logic for external signers, implementing uniqueness checks during registration, or optimizing the data structures within `CWallet` or its `ScriptPubKeyMan` instances that store and reference these signers. This prevents redundant entries and potential conflicts when interacting with external signing hardware.

prs.description: kernel:  add serialization method for btck_BlockHeader API
prs.author: yuvicc
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a serialization method for the `btck_BlockHeader` API within the Bitcoin Core Kernel, enabling the kernel to correctly handle and represent block header data. This is a crucial step for the foundational `btck` interface.
prs.technical_summary: This change implements functions to serialize and deserialize the `btck_BlockHeader` structure according to Bitcoin's consensus-critical serialization rules. This involves converting the in-memory C++ representation of a block header into a byte stream and vice-versa, adhering to little-endian ordering and specific data type sizes. This method is fundamental for the `btck` API to interact with the network, disk storage, and other components requiring byte-level block header data, ensuring data integrity and interoperability.

prs.description: wallet: Disallow wallet names that are paths including `..` and `.` elements
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR strengthens wallet security by preventing the use of specially crafted names that could exploit directory traversal vulnerabilities. It protects users from creating wallets in unintended or potentially malicious file system locations.
prs.technical_summary: This change introduces validation logic in the wallet creation and loading RPCs to explicitly disallow wallet names containing path traversal elements like `.` (current directory) and `..` (parent directory). By sanitizing wallet names, this prevents an attacker from creating or loading wallets outside the designated `wallets` subdirectory by manipulating the provided name, thereby mitigating potential file system access vulnerabilities and enhancing security.

prs.description: Update string and net utils for future HTTP operations
prs.author: pinheadmz
prs.public_summary: This PR updates string and networking utilities in preparation for future HTTP operations, enhancing Bitcoin Core's capabilities for broader communication needs. This lays the groundwork for more advanced network interactions.
prs.technical_summary: This change introduces or modifies utility functions related to string manipulation and network operations, specifically with an eye toward supporting HTTP communication. This might include additions for URL parsing, header manipulation, or more robust socket handling tailored for HTTP requests/responses. The aim is to create reusable components that will simplify the implementation of future HTTP-based features, promoting modularity and extensibility in the network communication layer.

prs.description: miniscript: Use valid script in test, etc (#31713 follow-ups)
prs.author: hodlinator
prs.public_summary: This PR improves Miniscript-related tests by ensuring they use valid scripts and addresses follow-up issues from a previous PR. It enhances the reliability and correctness of Miniscript functionality validation.
prs.technical_summary: Building on prior Miniscript integration work, this PR refines existing test cases by replacing invalid or suboptimal scripts with properly formed ones. It also resolves minor outstanding issues and inconsistencies identified in the original Miniscript implementation and its test suite. These targeted improvements ensure that the Miniscript test suite accurately reflects and thoroughly validates the intended behavior of Miniscript expressions.

prs.description: mining: always pad scriptSig at low heights, drop include_dummy_extranonce
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR refines Bitcoin Core's mining template generation by consistently padding the `scriptSig` for coinbase transactions at low block heights, and removes an outdated `include_dummy_extranonce` option. This simplifies mining operations and ensures correct `extranonce` space management for miners.
prs.technical_summary: The internal `getblocktemplate` logic is adjusted to always ensure sufficient `scriptSig` padding for the coinbase transaction at block heights below a certain threshold (e.g., pre-Taproot activation). This padding is crucial for miners to vary the `extranonce` and find valid block hashes. Concurrently, the `include_dummy_extranonce` configuration option is deprecated and removed, as the new consistent padding approach renders it obsolete, streamlining the mining interface.

prs.description: rpc: make getprivatebroadcastinfo and abortprivatebroadcast fail if privatebroadcast is not enabled
prs.author: polespinasa
prs.public_summary: This PR ensures that RPC commands related to 'private broadcasting' will fail gracefully and informatively if the feature is not explicitly enabled. This improves RPC robustness and provides clear feedback to users attempting to use unavailable functionality.
prs.technical_summary: This change adds an explicit verification check at the beginning of the `getprivatebroadcastinfo` and `abortprivatebroadcast` RPC handlers. These functions will now confirm that the 'privatebroadcast' feature (presumably controlled by a configuration flag) is enabled before proceeding with their core logic. If the feature is disabled, the RPC call will immediately return an appropriate error code, preventing execution of feature-specific code and providing a consistent failure mode for unimplemented functionality.

prs.description: validation: Ignore eventual error message from flushing in AcceptBlock
prs.author: optout21
prs.public_summary: This PR refines the block acceptance process by ignoring a specific, non-critical error message that may arise during database flushing. This prevents benign issues from being logged as errors and improves log clarity.
prs.technical_summary: During `AcceptBlock`, the node flushes uncommitted database changes. In certain scenarios, an 'eventual' error message can be generated by the database flush operation even if the overall process is successful or the error is inconsequential. This PR modifies the `AcceptBlock` error handling to explicitly disregard this specific message, ensuring it does not trigger unnecessary logging or interrupt the block validation flow, thus reducing false-positive error reports.

prs.description: ArgsManager: support command-specific options
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the `ArgsManager` to support options that are specific to individual RPC commands. This provides greater flexibility and clarity for users when configuring and interacting with Bitcoin Core's RPC interface.
prs.technical_summary: The `ArgsManager` is modified to allow registration and parsing of arguments that are scoped to particular RPC commands, rather than being globally applied. This likely involves extending the argument registration API to associate options with specific RPC method names, preventing conflicts and enabling more precise control over RPC behavior. This architectural improvement helps organize and manage the growing number of configuration options.

prs.description: coinselection: Tiebreak SRD eviction by weight
prs.author: murchandamus
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new tie-breaking rule for the "Single Random Draw" (SRD) coin selection algorithm, prioritizing the eviction of inputs by their transaction weight. This aims to improve the efficiency and fee-worthiness of generated transactions.
prs.technical_summary: Within the SRD coin selection algorithm, when multiple inputs are equally viable candidates for eviction (e.g., when trying to reduce transaction size without changing fee rate significantly), this change adds a secondary criterion. It modifies the eviction logic to sort or select inputs based on their weight contribution (e.g., vbytes), preferring to evict heavier inputs over lighter ones, in addition to other existing criteria. This results in more compact transactions.

prs.description: guix: Split manifest into build and codesign manifests
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the Guix build system by separating the manifest into distinct build and codesign components, enhancing clarity and maintainability for the reproducible build process. This improves the transparency and security auditing of official Bitcoin Core releases.
prs.technical_summary: The Guix build system previously used a monolithic manifest for both building Bitcoin Core binaries and performing the subsequent codesigning step. This PR splits this into two specialized manifest files: one specifically defining the build environment and dependencies, and another for the codesigning environment. This clear separation of concerns makes it easier to independently audit, update, and manage each stage of the reproducible build chain, improving overall system robustness.

prs.description: wallet: remove outdated arguments from chain scanning methods
prs.author: rkrux
prs.public_summary: This PR cleans up wallet code by removing obsolete and unnecessary arguments from internal chain scanning methods. This significantly improves code maintainability and simplifies the logic for how the wallet scans the blockchain.
prs.technical_summary: This PR involves a targeted refactor of the wallet's internal code, specifically addressing methods responsible for scanning the blockchain to identify relevant transactions (e.g., `CWallet::ScanForWalletTransactions`). It removes arguments from these methods that are no longer necessary, have become redundant due to prior architectural changes, or are now handled more efficiently through other internal wallet state mechanisms. This change simplifies function signatures, reduces potential for developer confusion, and enhances overall code clarity and long-term maintainability within the wallet's scanning infrastructure.

prs.description: blockstorage: Remove cs_LastBlockFile recursive mutex
prs.author: sedited
prs.public_summary: This PR removes a problematic recursive mutex, `cs_LastBlockFile`, from the block storage subsystem, improving the reliability and reducing the potential for deadlocks. It streamlines concurrency management within critical sections for better system stability.
prs.technical_summary: The `cs_LastBlockFile` recursive mutex was a source of potential issues due to its inherently complex locking semantics. This PR refactors the block storage logic, particularly around `CBlockFileInfo` and `CBlockFileSeq` management, to eliminate the necessity for a recursive mutex. This likely involves redesigning access patterns to shared block file resources, ensuring that non-recursive mutexes are used more precisely or that specific critical sections are accessed in a single-threaded manner.

prs.description: node: allocate index caches proportional to usage patterns
prs.author: svanstaa
prs.public_summary: This PR refines how index caches are allocated in the node, making their size proportional to actual usage patterns. This optimizes memory consumption by preventing over-allocation and ensuring resources are efficiently utilized.
prs.technical_summary: The node's memory management for index caches (e.g., UTXO set cache, block index cache) is enhanced to dynamically adjust allocation based on observed usage or configured heuristics. Instead of fixed-size allocations, the system now allocates memory more intelligently, potentially by analyzing the size of the chainstate or the number of transactions, ensuring memory is not wasted on underutilized caches.

prs.description: net: move cs_main up in FetchBlock to fix rpc assert crash
prs.author: Crypt-iQ
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves an RPC assertion crash by adjusting the locking order within the block fetching mechanism. This improves the overall stability of the node, particularly when RPC calls interact with block synchronization processes.
prs.technical_summary: This change addresses a critical bug where an RPC call could trigger an assertion crash due to an incorrect mutex locking order during block fetching. The fix involves moving the acquisition of `cs_main` (the global critical section protecting core blockchain state) earlier in the `FetchBlock` function within the networking subsystem. By acquiring `cs_main` before other potentially conflicting locks or operations, this PR ensures proper serialization of access to shared resources, thereby preventing race conditions and improving thread safety.

prs.description: rpc: replace ELISION references with explicit result fields
prs.author: satsfy
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the clarity and consistency of RPC responses by replacing implicit data 'elision' with explicit result fields. This makes RPC outputs more predictable and easier for developers to work with.
prs.technical_summary: RPC 'elision' refers to omitting fields from JSON responses if they are null, empty, or default. This PR modifies various RPC endpoints to explicitly include these fields in the JSON output, even if they hold null or default values. This involves updating the RPC serialization logic for affected commands to ensure that a consistent schema is always returned, reducing ambiguity and improving API predictability for client applications.

prs.description: fuzz: wallet: add target for `MigrateToDescriptor`
prs.author: brunoerg
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a fuzzing target for the `MigrateToDescriptor` wallet function, improving the robustness and security of wallet upgrades. Fuzz testing helps uncover edge cases and potential vulnerabilities in the migration process.
prs.technical_summary: A new fuzzing target is introduced specifically to test the `MigrateToDescriptor` function, which is responsible for converting legacy wallet data to descriptor-based formats. The fuzzer will generate a wide range of malformed or unexpected inputs for this function. This comprehensive testing aims to identify any crashes, hangs, or incorrect behavior that could arise during a wallet migration, thus enhancing the stability and security of the wallet subsystem.

prs.description: rpc, logging: add backgroundvalidation to getblockchaininfo
prs.author: polespinasa
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the `getblockchaininfo` RPC call by including information about any ongoing background validation processes. This provides users and monitoring tools with greater insight into the node's current state and activity.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the `getblockchaininfo` RPC response to include a new field, `backgroundvalidation`. This field will report the status or progress of any validation tasks running in the background, such as reindexing or block data consistency checks. It involves updating the RPC serialization logic and integrating the status from the relevant background processing components to expose this operational detail.

prs.description: Make deployment configuration available outside of regtest in unit tests
prs.author: darosior
prs.public_summary: This PR makes network deployment configurations available to unit tests beyond the regtest environment, simplifying the testing of soft fork logic. This improves the robustness and comprehensiveness of deployment-related tests across various network parameters.
prs.technical_summary: The change modifies the testing framework to allow unit tests to access and inspect `CDChainParams::GetConsensus().vDeployments` and other deployment-specific data for all networks, not just regtest. This typically involves adjusting how `CChainParams` objects are instantiated, mocked, or passed to test fixtures, enabling tests to accurately simulate conditions relevant to mainnet or testnet soft fork deployments without requiring a full network setup.

prs.description: rpc, wallet: add an option to not load the wallet after migrating
prs.author: polespinasa
prs.public_summary: This PR adds an option to prevent the automatic loading of a wallet after it has been migrated. This gives users greater control over wallet activation, enhancing flexibility and privacy.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, wallet migrations would automatically load the new wallet. This change introduces a configuration option that, when enabled, prevents the wallet management system from automatically loading a wallet after a successful migration. This involves modifying the wallet's post-migration startup logic to check for this new setting before attempting to load the wallet, ensuring the node operator has explicit control over wallet availability.

prs.description: fuzz: add ipc round-trip fuzz target
prs.author: enirox001
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new fuzzing target focused on the Inter-Process Communication (IPC) interface. This enhances the testing of IPC, improving the reliability and security of this communication channel.
prs.technical_summary: Fuzz testing involves providing unexpected or malformed inputs to software to discover vulnerabilities or crashes. This PR adds a dedicated fuzz target to exercise the complete 'round-trip' functionality of Bitcoin Core's IPC mechanism. It tests various message payloads and verifies responses, aiming to identify potential issues in the IPC serialization, deserialization, and message processing logic, thereby bolstering its robustness.

prs.description: test: Suppress another unsolicited `mock_process/*` output
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR suppresses unwanted output from `mock_process` during testing, making test logs cleaner and easier to read. It improves the developer experience by reducing noise in test environments.
prs.technical_summary: The `mock_process` utility, used within the test suite to simulate external processes, was generating unsolicited output that cluttered test logs. This change specifically targets and mutes this extraneous output from `mock_process` executions. By suppressing this noise, the test logs become more focused on relevant test results, improving the efficiency of debugging and test analysis for developers.

prs.description: wallet: fix `gethdkeys` RPC for descriptors with partial xprvs
prs.author: rkrux
prs.public_summary: This PR corrects an issue with the `gethdkeys` RPC command, ensuring it properly works with certain types of wallet descriptors. It improves the reliability of obtaining extended public and private key information for advanced wallet setups.
prs.technical_summary: The `gethdkeys` RPC command previously failed or returned incomplete information when attempting to extract hierarchical deterministic keys from wallet descriptors that included 'partial' extended private keys (xprvs). This PR updates the parsing and key extraction logic within the `Descriptor` and `HDChain` classes to correctly handle these partial xprvs, ensuring that all available key information can be reliably retrieved, even from complex descriptor structures.

prs.description: net: Fix Discover() not running when using -bind=0.0.0.0:port
prs.author: b-l-u-e
prs.public_summary: This fix ensures that Bitcoin Core correctly advertises its listen address to the network when configured to bind to all available network interfaces. It improves node discoverability and overall network connectivity for users binding to `0.0.0.0`.
prs.technical_summary: The `Discover()` function, responsible for advertising the node's listening address, was not being called when `-bind=0.0.0.0:port` was specified, leading to the node not announcing its actual reachable IP. This PR corrects the logic by ensuring that `Discover()` is invoked even when binding to the wildcard address. This allows the node to correctly identify and advertise its external IP address to peers, thereby improving its reachability on the network.

prs.description: test: Add importdescriptors rpc error coverage
prs.author: polespinasa
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the test suite for the `importdescriptors` RPC by adding coverage for error conditions. This ensures the RPC behaves correctly and robustly when invalid inputs or states are encountered.
prs.technical_summary: The existing RPC test suite for `importdescriptors` is expanded to include specific test cases that trigger various error paths. This involves invoking the RPC with malformed descriptors, insufficient permissions, incorrect parameters, or other scenarios designed to provoke expected error responses. The tests then assert that the correct error codes and messages are returned.

prs.description: bitcoin-cli: Add -ipcconnect option
prs.author: ryanofsky
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new `-ipcconnect` option for `bitcoin-cli`, allowing it to connect to the Bitcoin Core node via Inter-Process Communication (IPC). This provides a more efficient and potentially more secure local communication method compared to HTTP RPC.
prs.technical_summary: This change adds a new command-line argument to `bitcoin-cli`. When `-ipcconnect` is specified, `bitcoin-cli` will establish a connection to `bitcoind` using an IPC mechanism, such as a Unix domain socket or named pipe, instead of the default HTTP/TCP RPC. This requires implementing client-side IPC connection logic within `bitcoin-cli` to interact with `bitcoind`'s existing or newly exposed IPC server interface, reducing network overhead and improving latency for local interactions.

prs.description: kernel: guard btck::Handle move-assignment against self-move
prs.author: thomasbuilds
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a self-move guard to the `btck::Handle` move-assignment operator within the Bitcoin Kernel, preventing potential memory corruption. This improves the stability and reliability of the kernel's resource management.
prs.technical_summary: The PR enhances the `btck::Handle` move-assignment operator by explicitly checking for self-assignment (`this == &other`) at the beginning of the operator's implementation. This prevents an object from attempting to move its own resources to itself, which could lead to double-frees or invalid state if the source object's resources are prematurely released before being assigned to the destination. This is a standard C++ idiom for ensuring correctness and robustness in move operations.

prs.description: netif: fix compilation warning in QueryDefaultGatewayImpl()
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR addresses and resolves a compilation warning in the `QueryDefaultGatewayImpl()` function within the network interface code. Eliminating warnings improves code hygiene and ensures a cleaner build process.
prs.technical_summary: The fix typically involves a minor code adjustment, such as explicitly casting a variable to prevent a type mismatch warning, adding a `(void)` cast for unused parameters, or initializing a variable to suppress an uninitialized variable warning. The specific warning likely stemmed from a platform-specific compiler behavior or a subtle type interaction within the network interface implementation, now correctly resolved.

prs.description: ci: add OpenBSD Clang cross job
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a continuous integration (CI) job to build Bitcoin Core for OpenBSD using Clang. This helps ensure broader platform compatibility and robust testing for diverse environments.
prs.technical_summary: The change integrates a new workflow into the CI system that performs a cross-compilation of Bitcoin Core for OpenBSD using the Clang compiler. This involves configuring the appropriate toolchain and build flags within the CI environment, thereby expanding the matrix of tested build configurations. This job validates buildability on an additional tier-2 platform without requiring a native OpenBSD runner.

prs.description: wallet: rpc: Improve error message for low feerates.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 29.3.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 29.1.

highlights: **Mempool Policy:** The maximum number of potentially executed legacy signature operations in a single standard transaction is now limited to 2500.
**Mempool Policy:** The default minimum block feerate has been lowered to 1 satoshi per kvB, and default minimum relay and incremental relay feerates have been changed to 100 satoshis per kvB.
**Node Performance:** Unconditional logging to disk is now rate-limited to 1MiB per hour per source location.
**RPC:** The `dumptxoutset` RPC now requires a `type` parameter to be specified, with `latest` maintaining pre-v29.0 behavior.
**Node Stability:** The `-maxmempool` and `-dbcache` startup parameters are now capped on 32-bit systems to 500MB and 1GiB respectively.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 29.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core 29.0 integrates `assumeutxo` for mainnet, enhancing initial node synchronization speed. This version also features an updated P2P networking stack with built-in NATPMP/PCP, removal of the `mempoolfullrbf` option, and the introduction of "Ephemeral Dust" outputs for transaction policy. The build system has been fully migrated to CMake, and release binaries are now codesigned, bolstering security and simplifying development.
highlights: **Node Performance:** Bitcoin Core now includes an `assumeutxo` parameter for mainnet at block height 880,000, enabling significantly faster initial synchronization for new nodes.

**P2P Networking:** The `miniupnp` dependency has been removed, and an external `libnatpmp` library has been replaced with a built-in implementation of PCP and NAT-PMP, improving network connectivity and security.
**Mempool Policy:** "Ephemeral Dust" outputs are introduced, allowing a single zero-fee dust output in transactions provided it is spent within the same transaction package.
**Mempool Policy:** The `mempoolfullrbf` configuration option has been removed, establishing full replace-by-fee as the standard transaction replacement behavior.

**Build System:** The build system has been fully migrated to CMake with the legacy Autotools system removed, and macOS and Windows binaries are now codesigned and notarized to enhance release security.

prs.public_summary: This PR improves the wallet's stability by removing an internal assumption that could cause issues during blockchain reorganizations. This makes the wallet more resilient and robust when the network experiences temporary chain splits.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes an `Assume()` assertion from the wallet's internal logic that was found to be erroneous during blockchain reorganizations. This `Assume()` likely asserted a state that could be temporarily invalid during a reorg, potentially leading to crashes or incorrect behavior. Removing it allows the wallet to gracefully handle temporary chain inconsistencies without failing, improving its resilience to network reorg events.

prs.description: net processing: Add ibd check before processing block for txdownloadman
prs.author: sedited
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a crucial check to ensure the transaction download manager only processes blocks after the node has completed its initial block download (IBD). This prevents unnecessary processing and resource consumption during the critical synchronization phase.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces an `IsInitialBlockDownload()` check within the `TxDownloadMan`'s block processing pipeline. Before attempting to parse or request missing transactions from a newly received block, the `TxDownloadMan` now verifies that the node has exited IBD state. This optimization prevents the manager from performing resource-intensive operations on blocks that will soon be superseded or are not yet relevant to the synchronized chain, significantly reducing overhead during bootstrapping.

prs.description: kernel: Use enumeration type for flags argument
prs.author: TheCharlatan
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the Bitcoin Core kernel by replacing raw integer flags with a strong enumeration type for better code clarity and type safety. This makes the code easier to read and maintain, reducing the risk of errors from incorrect flag usage.
prs.technical_summary: It identifies functions within the `src/kernel` directory that use `int` or `unsigned int` for flags and replaces these with a newly defined `enum class`. This change enforces compile-time checking of flag values, preventing invalid combinations or accidental misuse of magic numbers, aligning with modern C++ best practices for the kernel abstraction layer.

prs.description: p2p: Advance pindexLastCommonBlock early after connecting blocks
prs.author: mzumsande
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes the peer-to-peer synchronization process by advancing the `pindexLastCommonBlock` earlier. This helps nodes more quickly determine shared block history with peers, speeding up initial block download and re-synchronization.
prs.technical_summary: The `pindexLastCommonBlock` tracks the highest block a peer is known to share. This PR modifies the P2P logic to advance this pointer immediately after a new block is connected, rather than waiting for subsequent P2P messages like `VERSION` or `VERACK`. By updating this marker proactively, the node can more accurately and swiftly assess its synchronized state with peers, which can reduce redundant block requests and improve the efficiency of the overall block download manager.

prs.description: p2p: send first addr self-announcement in separate message 🎄
prs.author: 0xB10C
prs.public_summary: This change improves how a Bitcoin node announces its own address to the network. By sending its address in a dedicated message, it helps other nodes discover and connect more efficiently.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the P2P protocol's initial connection handshake to send the node's first `addr` self-announcement in a separate, dedicated message. This ensures that the node's routable address is promptly received and processed by peers, facilitating quicker network discovery and reducing potential delays that could occur if the address were bundled with other initial messages, affecting `CNode` message handling.

prs.description: A few followups after introducing `/rest/blockpart/` endpoint
prs.author: romanz
prs.public_summary: This PR implements several follow-up improvements and fixes for the recently introduced `/rest/blockpart/` endpoint. These changes ensure the new API endpoint is more robust, reliable, and user-friendly for retrieving partial block data.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses minor issues and enhances the `/rest/blockpart/` REST endpoint, which allows fetching specific parts of a block, such as just the header or a range of transactions, rather than the entire block. It includes fixes for edge cases, improved error handling, and potentially minor performance tweaks directly related to serving partial block requests. These adjustments ensure correct and efficient data delivery, enhancing the usability and stability of the REST interface for developers and applications.

prs.description: Split `CWallet::Create()` into `CreateNew` and `LoadExisting`
prs.author: davidgumberg
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the wallet initialization process, cleanly separating the creation of new wallets from the loading of existing ones. This improves code clarity and maintainability for wallet lifecycle operations.
prs.technical_summary: This PR splits the `CWallet::Create()` static method into `CWallet::CreateNew()` and `CWallet::LoadExisting()`. `CreateNew()` is now solely responsible for initializing a new wallet instance and its associated state, while `LoadExisting()` handles deserialization and recovery from disk. This separation enhances the single responsibility principle, making wallet initialization paths more explicit, testable, and robust.

prs.description: miniscript: account for all `StringType` variants in `Miniscriptdescriptor::ToString()`
prs.author: pythcoiner
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes an issue in the Miniscript descriptor's `ToString()` method, ensuring it correctly handles all string type variants. This improves the reliability of descriptor serialization and prevents misrepresentation of Miniscript policies.
prs.technical_summary: The `Miniscriptdescriptor::ToString()` method is critical for serializing Miniscript descriptors into a canonical string format. This change modifies the implementation to ensure all `StringType` variants, which may involve different text encodings or handling of data, are correctly processed. The fix ensures comprehensive and accurate serialization across the full spectrum of valid Miniscript descriptor configurations, preventing potential data corruption or misinterpretation when descriptors are converted to strings.

prs.description: Musig2 tests
prs.author: w0xlt
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a comprehensive suite of tests for the Musig2 signature scheme. These tests ensure the correctness and reliability of any Musig2 implementation within Bitcoin Core.
prs.technical_summary: This pull request introduces a new set of unit and/or functional tests specifically targeting the Musig2 multi-signature scheme. The tests cover various aspects of Musig2, including key aggregation, generation of partial signatures, aggregation of partial signatures into a final aggregate signature, and its subsequent verification. This comprehensive testing ensures the cryptographic correctness and robustness of any integrated Musig2 primitives, covering both valid and edge-case scenarios.

prs.description: wallet: warn against accidental unsafe older() import
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This change adds a warning to protect users from accidentally importing potentially unsafe or deprecated `older()` script functions into their wallet. It helps users avoid security risks associated with this outdated scripting element.
prs.technical_summary: This PR implements a warning mechanism within the wallet's script import or descriptor parsing logic to detect and alert users if a script containing the `older()` function is being added. The `older()` function is often considered unsafe or has nuanced behavior in certain contexts, so this PR aims to prevent users from inadvertently using potentially problematic scripts by providing an explicit warning during wallet operations.

prs.description: mining: fix -blockreservedweight shadows IPC option
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes an issue where the `-blockreservedweight` command-line option would improperly override block template settings provided via IPC. It ensures that miners using IPC can reliably configure their reserved block weight, allowing for more flexible mining pool integrations.
prs.technical_summary: The issue involved a precedence bug where the `blockreservedweight` configuration from command-line arguments would unconditionally supersede values provided dynamically through the Inter-Process Communication (IPC) interface. This fix adjusts the configuration loading and merging logic to correctly prioritize or merge these settings. This ensures that IPC clients, such as external mining software, can effectively control block template parameters, resolving an unexpected behavior for miners.

prs.description: rpc: Handle -named argument parsing where '=' character is used
prs.author: zaidmstrr
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the RPC interface by correctly parsing arguments that contain an equals sign (`=`), particularly when using the `-named` argument style. This makes RPC commands more flexible and robust for developers interacting with structured parameters.
prs.technical_summary: The parsing logic for RPC arguments, likely within `src/rpc/util.cpp` or `src/rpc/client.cpp`, is enhanced to handle cases where a value for a named argument itself contains an equals character. The fix ensures that the string splitting or tokenization mechanism correctly distinguishes between the 'name=value' separator and an equals sign present within the value, allowing the full intended value to be passed accurately to the corresponding RPC method.

prs.description: ci: Add Windows + UCRT jobs for cross-compiling and native testing
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR expands the Continuous Integration (CI) system by adding new jobs for building and testing Bitcoin Core on Windows using the Universal C Runtime (UCRT). This enhances build reliability and compatibility for Windows developers.
prs.technical_summary: The CI configuration files (e.g., GitHub Actions workflows) are updated to include new matrix entries that set up build environments targeting Windows with UCRT. These jobs perform both cross-compilation from Linux and native compilation and testing directly on Windows runners, ensuring that the codebase remains compatible with modern Windows development toolchains and identifying potential platform-specific issues early.

prs.description: txgraph: drop move assignment operator
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR performs a minor code cleanup in the transaction graph component by removing an unnecessary move assignment operator. This refactoring improves code clarity and maintainability.
prs.technical_summary: The `txgraph` module's `TxGraph` class previously defined an explicit move assignment operator (`TxGraph::operator=(TxGraph&&)`). This change removes that definition, relying on either the compiler's default behavior or other existing mechanisms to handle object movement correctly. This simplification reduces boilerplate and aligns the code with modern C++ practices where explicit definition is often not required for such operators.

prs.description: coins: don't mutate main cache when connecting block
prs.author: andrewtoth
prs.public_summary: This PR refines how the UTXO set is updated during block connections by preventing direct mutation of the main coin cache. This improvement enhances the robustness and reliability of Bitcoin Core's UTXO management, especially during complex chain reorganizations.
prs.technical_summary: The change likely involves performing UTXO updates on a temporary or copy-on-write `CCoinsViewCache` layer during block connection. Only upon successful validation and commitment of the block are these changes atomically applied to the underlying main `CCoinsViewDB` or main `CCoinsViewCache`. This ensures that the global UTXO state remains consistent even if a block connection fails mid-process, preventing corruption or inconsistent states.

prs.description: contrib: update macOS SDK to Xcode-26.1.1-17B100
prs.author: fanquake
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the macOS Software Development Kit (SDK) used in the `contrib` build scripts to a newer version (Xcode-26.1.1-17B100). This ensures continued compatibility with modern macOS development environments and keeps the build process up-to-date for macOS contributors.
prs.technical_summary: The `contrib` directory houses various scripts and tools, including those for managing cross-compilation environments for different platforms. This change specifically targets the macOS SDK version employed in the build process for Apple platforms. By upgrading to Xcode-26.1.1-17B100, the build system benefits from updated compilers, libraries, and APIs, addressing potential deprecations and improving compatibility with recent macOS releases, which is essential for maintaining a robust and modern development workflow for macOS contributors.

prs.description: randomenv: Fix MinGW dllimport warning for `environ`
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR resolves a compilation warning specifically affecting MinGW users related to the `environ` global variable. This improves the build process on Windows systems using MinGW, leading to a cleaner development environment.
prs.technical_summary: The fix targets a `dllimport` warning encountered during compilation with MinGW on Windows, specifically concerning the `environ` global variable. The warning arises from an incorrect handling of `dllimport` for `environ` within the `randomenv` utility. The PR likely applies specific compiler directives or code adjustments to correctly declare or access `environ`, thereby suppressing the warning and ensuring correct linking and compilation.

prs.description: wallet: remove PreSelectedInputs and re-activate "AmountWithFeeExceedsBalance" error
prs.author: stratospher
prs.public_summary: This PR refines the wallet's coin selection by removing an experimental input strategy and re-enabling a crucial balance check. This improves the wallet's reliability in handling transaction fees and prevents overspending.
prs.technical_summary: This PR removes the `PreSelectedInputs` struct and its associated experimental coin selection logic. Concurrently, it re-activates the `AmountWithFeeExceedsBalance` error check within the wallet's transaction building process, ensuring that the total output amount plus calculated fee is rigorously compared against available UTXO balance, preventing attempts to construct transactions that overspend the wallet's funds.

prs.description: util: Abort on failing CHECK_NONFATAL in debug builds
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This change improves the debugging experience for Bitcoin Core developers by causing `CHECK_NONFATAL` failures to immediately abort the program in debug builds. This helps developers identify and resolve subtle issues earlier during development and testing.
prs.technical_summary: The behavior of the `CHECK_NONFATAL` macro is modified for debug builds; a failed assertion will now trigger `std::abort()` rather than merely logging the error. This change ensures that the program halts immediately upon detection of a non-fatal inconsistency. Developers can then attach a debugger at the precise point of failure, facilitating quicker root cause analysis and preventing execution with potentially corrupted states.

prs.description: mining: getCoinbase() returns struct instead of raw tx
prs.author: Sjors
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the `getCoinbase()` function within the mining module to return a structured data type instead of a raw transaction object. This improves code clarity, encapsulation, and maintainability by providing a more explicit and organized representation of coinbase transaction data.
prs.technical_summary: The `getCoinbase()` function's signature and implementation are updated to return a new dedicated `struct` (e.g., `CoinbaseTransactionData`) that encapsulates the necessary components of a coinbase transaction, such as the `CMutableTransaction` itself, and potentially other related metadata. This architectural change promotes data integrity by grouping related elements, reducing the likelihood of errors when handling coinbase-specific logic, and facilitating future extensions to the mining interface by providing a more robust internal API.

prs.description: init: point out -stopatheight may be imprecise
prs.author: brunoerg
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a clarification for the `-stopatheight` command-line option, informing users that the node's shutdown may not occur at the exact specified block height but rather shortly after. This sets more accurate user expectations.
prs.technical_summary: The modification updates the help text or introduces a startup log message associated with the `-stopatheight` argument. It explains that due to the asynchronous nature of block reception and processing, and the timing of shutdown checks, the node might process one or more blocks beyond the specified height before gracefully exiting. This is a documentation and user experience improvement rather than a functional change.

prs.description: Add a "tx output spender" index
prs.author: sstone
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces a new "transaction output spender" index, allowing users to efficiently query which transaction spent a particular unspent transaction output (UTXO). This enables advanced chain analysis and improves capabilities for wallet management and block explorers.
prs.technical_summary: The implementation involves adding a new database index layer that stores a mapping from `COutPoint` (transaction ID and output index) to the `COutPoint` of the spending transaction. This index is updated during block connection and disconnection, and new RPCs are introduced to query this data. This allows for quick lookups of spending transactions without scanning the entire blockchain.

prs.description: validation: periodically flush dbcache during reindex-chainstate
prs.author: andrewtoth
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces periodic flushing of the database cache during the `reindex-chainstate` operation, improving the robustness and reducing memory pressure during this potentially long process. This prevents excessive memory use and ensures progress is periodically saved to disk.
prs.technical_summary: When running `bitcoind` with `-reindex-chainstate`, the in-memory UTXO set cache (`dbcache`) can grow very large, leading to high memory consumption and potential out-of-memory (OOM) issues on systems with limited RAM. This change modifies the reindexing loop to periodically trigger a flush of the `dbcache` to disk. This is achieved by calling `FlushStateToDisk` via the `CValidationState` mechanism at regular intervals. The periodic flushing releases memory, ensures that partial progress is persisted to the database, making the reindex process more stable, resumable, and less prone to OOM errors.

prs.description: refactor, docs: Embedded ASMap [2/3]: Refactor asmap internals and add documentation
prs.author: fjahr
prs.public_summary: This PR, part two of three for embedding the ASMap, refactors the internal ASMap implementation and adds extensive documentation. This significantly improves the clarity and maintainability of Bitcoin Core's network-related components.
prs.technical_summary: Continuing the strategic initiative to embed the Autonomous System Map (ASMap) directly into the Bitcoin Core binary, this PR focuses on reorganizing the internal structures and algorithms responsible for ASMap management. This includes simplifying data loading, optimizing lookup procedures, and enhancing error handling. Crucially, comprehensive documentation is integrated to explain the design, usage, and maintenance of the embedded ASMap, which is vital for P2P network privacy and topological awareness, making the codebase more accessible for future development.

prs.description: p2p: add `DifferenceFormatter` fuzz target and invariant check
prs.author: frankomosh
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the robustness of Bitcoin Core's P2P networking code by adding a fuzz target and invariant check for the `DifferenceFormatter`. This improves the reliability and correctness of data serialization within the network layer, preventing potential issues.
prs.technical_summary: A new fuzz target is introduced specifically for the `DifferenceFormatter` component, which is critical for P2P message serialization and deserialization. Additionally, an invariant check is implemented to continually verify the internal consistency of the formatter's state during operation. This systematic testing and validation aim to uncover edge cases and subtle bugs, ensuring the integrity of P2P communication logic.

prs.description: Fix windows libc++ `fs::path` `fstream` compile errors
prs.author: ryanofsky
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes compilation errors on Windows systems that use `libc++` when interacting with `fs::path` and `fstream`. This broadens Bitcoin Core's compatibility, allowing it to be successfully built and run on more diverse Windows development setups.
prs.technical_summary: The compilation errors stemmed from an incompatibility when `std::filesystem::path` objects were directly used with `std::fstream` constructors or methods on Windows platforms employing the `libc++` standard library. The fix involves adapting the code to correctly convert `fs::path` instances to a compatible string type, such as `std::wstring`, which is appropriate for wide character handling on Windows, before passing them to `fstream`. This resolves the underlying type mismatch and enables successful compilation.

prs.description: kernel: doc: explain return value for `btck_WriteBytes` callback
prs.author: theStack
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the Bitcoin Kernel's documentation by clearly explaining the return values for the `btck_WriteBytes` callback function. This enhancement makes the kernel interface easier to understand and use for developers.
prs.technical_summary: The modification involves adding Doxygen-style comments to the declaration or definition of the `btck_WriteBytes` callback, specifically detailing the expected meaning and behavior associated with its integer return value. This clarifies whether the return signifies success, a specific error code, or the number of bytes written, which is crucial for correct integration and error handling.

prs.description: validation: do not wipe utxo cache for stats/scans/snapshots
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR prevents the unnecessary wiping of the UTXO cache during non-validation operations like generating statistics or creating snapshots. Keeping the cache intact improves efficiency for subsequent validation tasks.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, utility functions performing tasks like UTXO set statistics generation or database snapshot creation could inadvertently cause the `CCoinsViewCache` to be discarded or reset. This pull request modifies these specific code paths to avoid triggering cache invalidation mechanisms. By preserving the state of the UTXO cache, subsequent block or transaction validation processes can leverage the pre-existing in-memory data, reducing redundant disk I/O and improving overall system responsiveness.

prs.description: rpc: make `uptime` monotonic across NTP jumps
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the `uptime` RPC command by ensuring its reported value is always monotonically increasing, even when the system clock adjusts due to NTP synchronization. This provides a more reliable metric for how long the node process has been continuously running.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the implementation of the `uptime` RPC call to leverage a monotonic clock source, such as `std::chrono::steady_clock`, instead of a system wall clock. By relying on a clock guaranteed to only move forward, irrespective of NTP synchronizations or manual clock changes, the reported `uptime` will accurately reflect the continuous running duration of the Bitcoin Core process, preventing anomalous dips or jumps in the reported value.

prs.description: merkle: pre‑reserve leaves to prevent reallocs with odd vtx count
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes Merkle tree construction by pre-reserving memory for leaves, particularly when there's an odd number of transactions. This prevents costly memory reallocations during a core block operation.
prs.technical_summary: Merkle tree construction, especially when dealing with an odd number of transaction leaves, can incur performance penalties due to `std::vector` reallocations when a dummy leaf is added to balance the tree. This PR addresses this by explicitly calling `reserve()` on the internal data structure (e.g., `std::vector<uint256>`) that stores the Merkle leaves. It pre-allocates enough capacity for `vtx.size()` plus one additional element if `vtx.size()` is odd, thereby eliminating unnecessary memory reallocations and improving CPU cache efficiency during block processing.

prs.description: kernel: revert accidentally removed copyright header
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR addresses a minor oversight by restoring an accidentally removed copyright header in a kernel module file. It's a small cleanup to maintain proper attribution and licensing within the codebase.
prs.technical_summary: This change specifically identifies a file within the `kernel` directory where a standard Bitcoin Core copyright header was inadvertently removed in a prior commit. The PR simply adds the correct copyright boilerplate back to the top of the file. This ensures compliance with project licensing and attribution requirements without altering any functional code, preserving intellectual property metadata.

prs.description: kernel: add btck_block_tree_entry_equals
prs.author: stickies-v
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the `kernel` library by introducing a new function to compare block tree entries. This provides a precise way to check if two block entries are identical, which is vital for internal consistency and future modularity.
prs.technical_summary: The `kernel` library, a key component for core blockchain logic, gains `btck_block_tree_entry_equals` with this change. This function is designed to perform a robust comparison of two `CBlockTreeEntry` objects, likely by comparing their block hashes, heights, and other critical metadata. This ensures accurate equality checks within the block tree, supporting data integrity validations and facilitating future architectural changes within the kernel.

prs.description: [IBD] coins: increase default UTXO flush batch size to 32 MiB
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR significantly boosts initial block download (IBD) performance by increasing the default batch size for flushing UTXO data to disk. This helps nodes sync faster, especially on systems with fast storage.
prs.technical_summary: It modifies the `CCoinsViewCache` or related components to increase the `DEFAULT_FLUSH_BATCH_SIZE` from a smaller value to 32 MiB. This allows more modified UTXO entries to accumulate in memory before being written to disk in a single batch, reducing the frequency of disk I/O operations and improving throughput during IBD, particularly for LevelDB backend interactions.

prs.description: wallet: Always rewrite tx records during migration
prs.author: achow101
prs.public_summary: This PR ensures that all transaction records are consistently rewritten during wallet database migrations, preventing potential data inconsistencies. This improves the robustness and reliability of wallet upgrades, guaranteeing correct transaction data formatting across versions.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the wallet's database migration logic to explicitly enforce a rewrite operation on all stored transaction records (`CTransactionRecord`). This guarantees that even if a record appears superficially valid, it is re-serialized according to the latest schema definitions during a migration. This systematic approach ensures data integrity and consistency, preventing subtle bugs that could arise from legacy record formats persisting across wallet versions.

prs.description: refactor: Improve assumeutxo state representation
prs.author: ryanofsky
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the internal representation of the `assumeutxo` state, a feature designed to speed up initial block download by starting from a pre-computed UTXO set. This improvement enhances the clarity, maintainability, and efficiency of this crucial mechanism.
prs.technical_summary: The refactoring focuses on optimizing the data structures and logic used to store and manage the `assumeutxo` state, particularly how checkpoint data and related metadata are represented in memory and serialized to disk. This might involve consolidating state variables, leveraging more efficient data types, or clarifying the transitions between different `assumeutxo` states. The aim is to make the `assumeutxo` implementation more robust, easier to extend, and more performant, directly contributing to faster and more reliable initial syncs.

prs.description: init: Require explicit -asmap filename
prs.author: ryanofsky
prs.public_summary: This PR mandates that users explicitly provide a filename when using the `-asmap` argument. This clarifies configuration requirements for Autonomous System mapping, reducing user errors and ensuring transparency regarding the map file used for peer selection.
prs.technical_summary: The argument parsing logic within `src/init.cpp` or `src/util/system.cpp` is updated to require a value for the `-asmap` command-line option. If `-asmap` is specified without an accompanying filename, the system will now produce an error or warning, preventing silent misconfigurations. This ensures that the `ASMap` functionality, which aids in geographically diverse peer connections, always operates with an explicitly defined and known map file.

prs.description: log: print every script verification state change
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR adds detailed logging for every change in script verification state, providing valuable insights for debugging and understanding transaction validation failures. This can be crucial for developers investigating complex transaction issues or new script features.
prs.technical_summary: It modifies the script interpreter (`CScriptInterpreter`) to emit verbose log messages (e.g., using `LogPrint` with a new category) whenever the script execution state changes. This includes pushing/popping items from the stack, executing opcodes, or encountering errors, offering a step-by-step trace of script execution for advanced debugging purposes when enabled.

prs.description: util: Remove brittle and confusing sp::Popen(std::string)
prs.author: maflcko
prs.public_summary: This PR removes a problematic `Popen` overload that was prone to shell injection vulnerabilities and confusing usage. Its removal improves the security and clarity of external process execution within Bitcoin Core.
prs.technical_summary: The `sp::Popen(std::string)` overload, which implicitly uses a shell to execute its argument, is deprecated and removed. Developers are now encouraged or forced to use `sp::Popen(std::vector<std::string>)`, which directly executes a command and its arguments without invoking a shell. This mitigates potential command injection risks and ensures explicit command specification.

prs.description: kernel: Add block header support and validation
prs.author: yuvicc
prs.public_summary: This is a foundational PR for the 'Kernel' project, adding support and validation for block headers. It modularizes critical validation logic, paving the way for a more robust and flexible architecture.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a dedicated 'kernel' module or subsystem responsible for block header processing. It extracts existing block header parsing, serialization, and initial validation logic (e.g., proof-of-work checks, timestamp rules, Merkle root verification) from the monolithic validation component into this new, more isolated module. This forms a crucial step in the 'Kernel' strategic initiative, aiming to establish clear architectural boundaries and facilitate a more modular, testable, and maintainable codebase for consensus-critical logic.

prs.description: validation: add reusable coins view for ConnectBlock
prs.author: andrewtoth
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes the block connection process by introducing a reusable coins view. This enhancement reduces redundant object creation and destruction, significantly speeding up node synchronization.
prs.technical_summary: The `ConnectBlock` function currently allocates a new `CCoinsViewCache` for each block being connected, leading to repetitive memory overhead. This PR refactors `ConnectBlock` to accept and utilize a `CCoinsViewCache` instance passed by reference, allowing for its reuse across multiple block connections. This optimization minimizes object construction/destruction cycles and cache thrashing, particularly benefiting Initial Block Download (IBD) by reducing CPU and memory overhead during sequential block processing.

prs.description: kernel: Expose reusable `PrecomputedTransactionData` in script validation
prs.author: joshdoman
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances script validation by exposing and making reusable `PrecomputedTransactionData` within the kernel for validation functions. This optimization avoids redundant computations during transaction validation, leading to faster processing and improved overall node performance, especially for blocks with many transactions.
prs.technical_summary: The change modifies the script validation interface within the `src/kernel` to accept and utilize a `PrecomputedTransactionData` object, which encapsulates expensive-to-compute data such as signature hashes. Instead of recalculating these values repeatedly for each signature check within a transaction, they are now computed once and passed to validation functions. This architectural change reduces the computational overhead of `CheckInputScripts` and similar validation functions, significantly improving transaction processing throughput and making the kernel's validation components more modular and efficient.

prs.description: refactor: unify container presence checks
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the codebase to unify and standardize how checks for element presence in various containers are performed. This improves code consistency, readability, and reduces potential for subtle bugs across the project.
prs.technical_summary: The refactoring identifies disparate patterns, such as `map.count(key)` versus `map.find(key) != map.end()`, used across the codebase for checking if an element exists within standard library containers like `std::map` or `std::set`. It unifies these checks to a consistent idiom, likely preferring `map.contains(key)` where available (C++20) or a standardized `find` pattern. This eliminates redundancy, simplifies future maintenance, and promotes a more robust coding style.

prs.description: p2p: Allow block downloads from peers without snapshot block after assumeutxo validation
prs.author: stringintech
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the peer-to-peer network's flexibility, allowing nodes to download blocks from peers even if they don't advertise snapshot support after initial assumeutxo validation. This enhances network connectivity and reduces potential bottlenecks during synchronization.
prs.technical_summary: This PR adjusts the P2P block download logic to be more lenient regarding the `NODE_ASSUMEUTXO` service bit after a node has already validated its initial `assumeutxo` snapshot. It relaxes the requirement to only download from peers advertising this bit once the local `assumeutxo` chain state is established, allowing block downloads from any capable peer. This improves peer selection and block propagation efficiency in certain network topologies by broadening the pool of available block sources.

prs.description: merkle: migrate `path` arg to reference and drop unused args
prs.author: l0rinc
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors internal Merkle tree computation functions by optimizing argument passing and removing unused parameters. This improves code efficiency and clarity by avoiding unnecessary data copying and simplifying function signatures.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 27.3.
release_summary: This release continues the modernization of the wallet system by removing legacy format support and migrating existing non-HD keys to descriptor-based management. Network integrity and privacy received enhancements through witness checks and improved Tor integration, while performance optimizations were introduced in the mempool and database. Key updates to RPC functionality and a transition to Qt 6 for the build system are also included.
highlights: **Wallet:** Support for creating and loading legacy wallet formats has been removed, with existing non-HD keys now migrated to `combo()` descriptors, and an in-memory UTXO tracking system implemented for efficiency.

**P2P & Security:** Network integrity was enhanced by adding a witness mutation check into the `FillBlock` function; Tor privacy was improved by preventing accidental circuit sharing and not applying whitelist permissions to onion inbounds.

**Mempool & Policy:** The default mempool policy now allows data-carrying outputs (OP_RETURNs) larger than 83 bytes, and significant experimental work on the cluster mempool continued with the introduction of the TxGraph data structure and reorg functionality.

**RPC:** The `bumpfee` and `psbtbumpfee` RPC commands now support full Replace-By-Fee (RBF) transactions, a `getdescriptoractivity` RPC command was added, and the `rpcuser`/`rpcpassword` options were undeprecated with hashed credentials.

**Build System:** Bitcoin Core's graphical interface now utilizes Qt 6, and core P2P performance was improved by avoiding unnecessary transaction iterations during Initial Block Download and reorgs, and by enhancing orphan transaction resolution.

prs.description: wallet, refactor: Remove Legacy check and error

This simplifies the wallet's logic, reduces technical debt, and makes the codebase easier to maintain without impacting current wallet functionality.

prs.description: policy: uncap datacarrier by default
prs.author: instagibbs
