prs.technical_summary: This change involves identifying and removing code paths related to parsing, storing, and connecting to Tor v2 `.onion` addresses. This includes modifications to the `CNetAddr` class, address manager (`addrman`), and P2P connection logic to no longer recognize or attempt to establish connections with v2 addresses. The removal streamlines the network stack, reduces potential attack surface from deprecated protocols, and focuses resources on supporting the more secure and resilient Tor v3 services.

prs.description: Add I2P support using I2P SAM
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR integrates native support for I2P (Invisible Internet Project) into Bitcoin Core, allowing nodes to communicate over this anonymous network. This provides enhanced privacy options for users seeking greater anonymity when running their Bitcoin node.
prs.technical_summary: The PR introduces a new networking transport layer within Bitcoin Core designed for I2P connections, leveraging the I2P SAM (Simple Anonymous Messaging) protocol. The implementation involves creating an I2P-specific `NetGroup`, handling I2P addresses (likely extending `CService`), and adapting the peer discovery and message serialization/deserialization logic to operate over I2P's stream-based anonymity layer. This enables Bitcoin Core nodes to establish and maintain connections with other I2P peers.

prs.description: Torv2 removal followups
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR contains follow-up changes to complete the removal of Torv2 support from Bitcoin Core. It cleans up remaining code paths to ensure full alignment with Torv3, improving network compatibility and security.
prs.technical_summary: This PR systematically removes any lingering code, configuration, or logic specifically tied to Torv2 addresses and services within the codebase. This includes updating network advertising logic, address parsing, and potentially GUI elements that previously differentiated Torv2. The objective is to fully eliminate support for the deprecated Torv2 protocol, streamlining the codebase and exclusively enforcing the use of the more secure and modern Torv3.

prs.description: net: relay I2P addresses even if not reachable (by us)
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the I2P network's peer discovery by allowing Bitcoin Core nodes to relay I2P addresses even if they cannot directly connect to them. This fosters a more robust and interconnected I2P routing layer.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the network's address relaying policy to permit the relay of I2P addresses received from peers, irrespective of whether the local node itself has successfully established a connection to that I2P destination. This relaxation in policy enhances the propagation of I2P peer information, contributing to a more comprehensive and resilient I2P address discovery mechanism across the network, even if direct reachability verification is not performed by the relaying node.

prs.description: Well-defined CAddress disk serialization, and addrv2 anchors.dat
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR refines how network addresses are saved to disk, ensuring they are consistently handled and enabling support for a newer, more flexible address format. This improves network reliability and future-proofs address storage.
prs.technical_summary: This PR formalizes the disk serialization of `CAddress` objects, specifically addressing `addrv2` (BIP155) support in `anchors.dat`. It ensures that `CAddress` objects are always written and read with a consistent versioning scheme, allowing for both `addrv1` and `addrv2` addresses to be stored and retrieved reliably. The change likely involves updating the serialization logic for `CAddress` to include a version byte and adapt existing file formats (like `anchors.dat`) to handle the variable-length `addrv2` format, preventing data corruption and enabling a seamless upgrade path for network peers.

prs.description: net: don't bind on 0.0.0.0 if binds are restricted to Tor
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances privacy by preventing Bitcoin Core from binding to all network interfaces (`0.0.0.0`) when connections are restricted exclusively to Tor. It ensures that the node doesn't inadvertently expose itself on clear-net interfaces.
prs.technical_summary: This PR refines the network binding logic to prevent the node from attempting to bind a listening socket to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) if the configuration explicitly restricts network activity to Tor-only. This ensures that when `onlynet=tor` is specified, the node will not accidentally open a listening port on clear-net interfaces, mitigating privacy risks and enforcing the intended network isolation.

prs.description: net: Add Tor v3 hardcoded seeds
prs.author: laanwj
prs.public_summary: This PR improves Bitcoin Core's ability to connect to the Tor network by adding new hardcoded seeds that support Tor v3 onion services. This enhances initial connection reliability and strengthens privacy for users operating nodes over Tor.
prs.technical_summary: The PR updates the static list of hardcoded network seeds to include new Tor v3 onion service addresses. Hardcoded seeds serve as initial contact points for a Bitcoin Core node to discover peers when it has no prior connection history. Integrating v3 seeds ensures better bootstrapping capabilities for Tor-connected nodes, supporting the latest, more secure Tor onion service protocol and improving network resilience.

prs.description: p2p, refactor: make NetPermissionFlags an enum class
prs.author: jonatack
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the internal `NetPermissionFlags` in the peer-to-peer networking code to use a C++ `enum class`. This improves type safety and code clarity, making it less prone to errors and easier for developers to maintain.
prs.technical_summary: This change converts the `NetPermissionFlags` enumeration, which defines various network peer permission levels (e.g., `PF_RELAY`, `PF_BLOCKSONLY`), from a plain `enum` to an `enum class` (scoped enumeration). This refactoring enhances type safety by preventing implicit conversions to integers and avoids name collisions within the global namespace. It requires explicit qualification for enum members (e.g., `NetPermissionFlags::Relay`), making the code more robust and self-documenting for engineers working on the P2P layer.

prs.description: addrman: improve performance by using more suitable containers
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR significantly improves the performance of Bitcoin Core's address manager (`addrman`), which stores known peer addresses for connecting to the network. By optimizing the underlying data structures, it makes operations like adding and retrieving peer information much faster and more efficient.
prs.technical_summary: This PR refactors the `CAddrMan` class by replacing existing data structures, likely `std::list` or less optimal `std::set`/`std::map` implementations, with more performance-tuned containers such as `std::unordered_map` or `std::vector` combined with efficient search algorithms. This change specifically targets frequently accessed operations within `addrman`, such as finding known addresses, adding new ones, or selecting addresses for connection attempts. The goal is to reduce algorithmic complexity and constant factors, leading to lower CPU utilization and improved responsiveness for network-related tasks.

prs.description: banman: save the banlist in a JSON format on disk
prs.author: vasild
prs.public_summary: This PR updates the `banman` component to save the node's banlist in a human-readable JSON format, making it easier for users and administrators to inspect and manage blocked peer addresses. This improves the transparency and manageability of network bans.
prs.technical_summary: This commit refactors the `banman` module to serialize and deserialize the list of banned peer addresses using JSON, replacing a potentially less structured or proprietary format. It involves modifying the `banman`'s storage methods, likely within `banman.cpp` and `banman.h`, to utilize a JSON serialization library for writing to and reading from the `banlist.json` file. This change provides a standardized and easily parsable format, facilitating external tools' interaction with the banlist and simplifying debugging for node operators. A migration path is typically included to handle existing banlist formats upon upgrade.

prs.description: net: Add NAT-PMP port forwarding support
prs.author: hebasto
prs.public_summary: This PR adds support for NAT-PMP (Network Address Translation Port Mapping Protocol) to Bitcoin Core. It allows nodes behind certain types of routers to automatically open ports, making it easier for them to accept incoming connections and contribute to the network's health.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a new component within the networking subsystem to interact with NAT-PMP capable routers. It implements the NAT-PMP protocol client, enabling the node to send requests to the router's gateway for mapping external ports to its internal listening port. This is achieved by sending UDP requests (e.g., Port Mapping Request) to the gateway's well-known NAT-PMP port and handling responses. The implementation likely leverages existing `ThreadSocketHandler` or similar networking abstractions to manage asynchronous NAT-PMP communication alongside other network operations, including periodic mapping refreshes.

prs.description: Add support for inferring tr() descriptors
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR adds crucial support for inferring `tr()` descriptors, which are used to represent Taproot outputs, making it easier for wallets to correctly identify and manage funds sent to Taproot addresses. prs.technical_summary: This PR implements logic within the descriptor parser and wallet codebase to correctly identify and generate `tr()` (Taproot) descriptors from script templates or transaction outputs. It involves extending the `Descriptor` class or related parsing utilities to recognize Taproot-specific script patterns, derive `xpub` or `xpriv` information, and construct the appropriate descriptor string. This enables wallets to automatically infer Taproot addresses and manage keys associated with these outputs, streamlining Taproot adoption for users and developers. This functionality is vital for making Taproot funds manageable within a descriptor-based wallet.

prs.description: p2p: Protect last outbound HB compact block peer
prs.author: sdaftuar
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the peer-to-peer network by preventing Bitcoin Core from inadvertently disconnecting from its last remaining outbound peer that supports compact block relay. This helps maintain crucial network connectivity, especially during initial synchronization or periods of low peer count.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces logic to prevent the eviction or disconnection of the last `outbound-full-relay` peer that also supports compact block relay (BIP152). Previously, such a peer could be undesirably disconnected, impacting critical block propagation. The change modifies peer management strategies, likely within `CConnman::AttemptToEvictPeer()` or similar eviction logic, to add an exception for this specific peer type, ensuring its persistence to maintain efficient block propagation even when peer slots are scarce.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.21.2.
release_summary: This release of Bitcoin Core version 0.21.2 focuses on significant improvements to the peer-to-peer network for enhanced reliability, performance, and resilience. Key updates also include stability and accuracy improvements for the wallet and an important enhancement to the macOS build process.
highlights: **P2P Network:** Peer discovery, selection, and overall network connectivity are improved through reductions in unusable addresses, optimizations in peer management functions, preventing unnecessary disconnections, and defaulting to `NODE_WITNESS` in announced services.

**P2P Security & Reliability:** Node resilience is strengthened by rate-limiting unverified address propagation, preventing crashes from corrupted address data, ensuring graceful error reporting for invalid peer data files, and fixing critical initialization order bugs.
**Wallet:** Wallet functionality is improved with more accurate descriptor inference by resetting scan progress, and enhanced robustness against file system access errors during directory iteration.
**Build System:** The reproducible build process for macOS is enhanced by implementing a custom code signing tool, which ensures the integrity and authenticity of executables.

prs.description: p2p: Rename fBlocksOnly, Add test
prs.author: MarcoFalke

If the `peers.dat` file is found to be malformed or corrupted, an `InitError` is now immediately raised. This prevents the node from continuing startup with an inconsistent or potentially harmful peer list, providing a clear error indication to the user and avoiding subsequent network issues.

prs.description: addrman: Avoid crash on corrupt data, Force Check after deserialize

This `Check()` performs an integrity validation on the loaded data; if corruption is detected, the `addrman` is reset. This design prevents undefined behavior and allows the node to rebuild its address book safely.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.21.1.
release_summary: This release primarily focuses on the technical implementation required for the upcoming Taproot soft fork, including its activation parameters and the new Bech32m address format. Additionally, it features security enhancements for wallet RPCs, architectural improvements for signature validation, and increased robustness in network message processing.
highlights: **Consensus:** Included mainnet and testnet activation parameters for the Taproot soft fork (BIP 341), which utilizes Speedy Trial signaling for activation and integrates support for Schnorr signatures (BIP 340) and Tapscript (BIP 342).
**RPC:** Implemented BIP 350 Bech32m encoding, which modifies RPC behavior for v1+ Segwit addresses to require and use Bech32m encoding.
**Wallet:** Enhanced security by preventing `sendtoaddress` and `sendmany` RPC commands when wallets are configured without private keys.
**Wallet:** Introduced `DeferredSignatureChecker`, an architectural improvement for more flexible and efficient signature validation.
**P2P:** Improved robustness of network message processing by resolving a potential undefined behavior warning detected by UBSan.

If a sufficient supermajority of blocks signal their support, Taproot will lock-in and subsequently activate at a predetermined future block height, introducing Schnorr signatures, Tapscript, and other significant protocol enhancements.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.21.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core version 0.21.0 integrates foundational support for future protocol upgrades, introduces significant enhancements to P2P networking and user privacy, and implements architectural improvements to wallet management. The release further focuses on strengthening the node's security posture and improving wallet data integrity.
highlights: **Consensus:** Validation rules for Schnorr signatures, Taproot (BIP341), and Tapscript (BIP342) have been implemented, enabling advanced scripting capabilities.
**P2P:** Full support for Tor v3 hidden services has been added through BIP155, enhancing network privacy and security for Tor users.
**Wallet:** SQLite has been introduced as an optional, alternative database backend for new descriptor wallets, offering enhanced reliability and preparing for future features.
**P2P:** The mempool now tracks locally submitted transactions separately, preventing them from being easily linked to the originating node through standard mempool queries.
**Build System:** Modern compiler hardening flags have been added to protect Bitcoin Core executables against memory-corruption attacks, significantly enhancing the security posture of running nodes.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.20.1.
release_summary: This release primarily focuses on refining peer management, enhancing PSBT compatibility and accuracy, and correcting a mining template RPC error. It includes critical bug fixes and improvements to core functionality, improving network resilience and transaction processing reliability.
highlights: **P2P:** The automatic peer banning mechanism has been replaced with a discouragement filter, which alters how misbehaving nodes are handled.
**Mining:** The `GetBlockTemplate` RPC now accurately includes `!segwit` and `csv` in the 'rules' key, providing correct consensus rule information for mining.
**PSBT:** Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions (PSBTs) now permit both `non_witness_utxo` and `witness_utxo` fields for SegWit inputs, enhancing compatibility.
**RPC:** PSBT decoding logic was corrected to ensure input value sums are incremented only once per UTXO, preventing miscalculations in transaction fee determination.

prs.description: Replace automatic bans with discouragement filter
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR refines Bitcoin Core's peer management by replacing automatic bans with a more nuanced discouragement filter. This change aims to improve network connectivity and resilience by handling misbehaving peers more gracefully, reducing unnecessary disconnections.
prs.technical_summary: This PR fundamentally alters the peer-to-peer network's misbehavior handling mechanism. It replaces the previous system, which would outright ban peers based on certain infractions, with a more sophisticated "discouragement filter." Instead of immediate bans, the filter assigns a discouragement score to peers, leading to a temporary reduction in connectivity or delayed reconnection attempts without permanent severance. This approach mitigates the risk of network partitioning or denial-of-service by making the node more resilient to minor or transient peer issues, improving overall network health.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.20.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core 0.20.0 focuses on significant security enhancements, P2P network improvements, and key RPC and wallet functionality updates. The release removes several legacy dependencies and protocols to streamline the codebase and improve security. It also introduces new features like a UTXO snapshot tool and enhances network resilience through improved peer diversity.
highlights: **Build System, Security:** OpenSSL dependency has been removed, with cryptographic functions replaced by minimal, audited libraries to reduce the attack surface.
**RPC:** A new `dumptxoutset` RPC command has been added, allowing users to create a snapshot of the entire Unspent Transaction Output (UTXO) set.
**P2P:** The peer-to-peer layer now supports `asmap` for grouping IP addresses by Autonomous System, improving peer diversity and network robustness.
**Wallet:** New wallets now default to generating native SegWit (bech32) addresses, which enhances privacy and reduces transaction fees.
**Security, P2P:** Support for the deprecated BIP61 reject network messages and the legacy BIP70 payment protocol has been removed.

This PR changes the internal computation to work with `absolute_fee` values (e.g., total satoshis for a transaction, derived from rate and virtual size), ensuring more precise and deterministic filtering behavior across the network by standardizing on a clear minimum absolute fee. This avoids potential discrepancies due to differing size calculations or floating point inaccuracies.

prs.description: gui: Set CConnman byte counters earlier to avoid uninitialized reads
prs.author: ryanofsky
prs.public_summary: This is a bug fix for the graphical user interface, ensuring that network traffic counters are correctly initialized before being displayed. It prevents the GUI from showing incorrect or garbage values for sent and received data, providing accurate network statistics to the user.
prs.technical_summary: This PR resolves an initialization bug within the GUI's display of network statistics. The issue stemmed from the `CConnman`'s byte counters, such as `nBytesSent` and `nBytesRecv`, not being explicitly initialized to zero at instantiation. This omission could lead to undefined behavior or the display of arbitrary, uninitialized values in the user interface for network traffic. The fix ensures these counters are properly zero-initialized during `CConnman`'s construction, guaranteeing the GUI consistently presents accurate and meaningful network usage statistics to the user.

prs.description: net processing: Only send a getheaders for one block in an INV
prs.author: jnewbery
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes network traffic by requesting headers for only one block at a time when an INV message advertises multiple new blocks. It improves network efficiency and reduces unnecessary data transfer during initial block synchronization.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, when receiving an `INV` message advertising multiple new blocks, the node would send a `getheaders` request covering all advertised blocks. This change modifies the `net processing` logic to only send a `getheaders` request for the *first* unknown block advertised in the `INV` message. This prevents redundant `getheaders` requests, as the response for the first block will typically include subsequent blocks in the chain, leading to more efficient header synchronization.

prs.description: Use rolling bloom filter of recent block txs for AlreadyHave() check
prs.author: sdaftuar
prs.public_summary: This feature improves how Bitcoin Core quickly checks if it has already seen a transaction from a peer. It uses an efficient filter to avoid re-requesting recent transactions, saving bandwidth and processing power.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a `rolling bloom filter` mechanism to optimize the `AlreadyHave()` check for incoming transaction inventory messages. Instead of immediately querying the mempool or disk, a probabilistic bloom filter, populated with transaction IDs from recently connected blocks, is consulted first. This allows for a fast, memory-efficient probabilistic check that significantly reduces the necessity for more expensive database lookups or full mempool scans, thereby decreasing network bandwidth consumption from redundant requests and lowering CPU overhead for transaction processing.

This PR removes this redundant field, streamlining the `CValidationState` structure and its associated error-handling mechanisms. The change simplifies the interface for functions like `IsValidState` and `IsInvalid` by focusing solely on valid/invalid states, without an unused intermediate `REJECT` enum, thus making the validation outcome clearer.

The implementation likely introduces or enhances a check against the node's rejection cache or mempool status before initiating any relay attempt. This optimization reduces wasted bandwidth and CPU cycles across the network by preventing the propagation of transactions that are known to be invalid, thus improving overall network efficiency and reducing unnecessary peer workload.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.19.2.
release_summary: This release primarily focuses on significant peer-to-peer network infrastructure updates and internal code hardening. It includes foundational work for future network capabilities, security enhancements across various subsystems, and introduces a new test network for development. Several consensus-related fixes and refactors are also integrated to improve stability and determinism.
highlights: **Consensus/Testing:** Implemented Signet (BIP-325), a new test network providing a stable and controlled environment for testing Bitcoin features.
**P2P:** Added support for the new ADDRv2 network address format (BIP155), enabling communication and storage of a broader range of IP address types.
**P2P:** Updated the transaction relay mechanism to use 'wtxid' for transactions containing witness data, improving the efficiency and security of SegWit transaction propagation.
**P2P/Privacy:** Introduced foundational support for compact block filters (BIP157/BIP158), enabling nodes to signal support, request, and serve filter headers and checkpoints.

**Consensus:** Refactored cryptographic hash computation for transaction validation and fixed potential undefined behavior in the script interpreter to ensure deterministic script execution and safer script code.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.19.1.
release_summary: This release of Bitcoin Core version 0.19.1 addresses various technical issues across several components. It includes enhanced robustness for wallet transaction handling and resolves specific bugs within the RPC and ZeroMQ interfaces. Furthermore, the build system has been updated to support newer dependency versions.
highlights: **Wallet:** Improved Partially Signed Bitcoin Transaction (PSBT) handling to gracefully manage PSBTs containing unspendable inputs, preventing related errors.
**RPC:** Corrected the `bumpfee` RPC call to accurately return the original transaction fee when a feerate argument is specified.
**ZMQ:** Fixed issues in the ZeroMQ (ZMQ) interface concerning invalid arguments and multiple notifiers, enhancing notification reliability for external applications.
**Build System:** Resolved a critical build issue, allowing Bitcoin Core to compile successfully with the Boost 1.72.0 library.

The modification ensures that all exceptions caught within this critical path are explicitly logged under the designated `net` logging category. This change provides more granular control over log filtering and analysis, making it substantially easier for developers to pinpoint, diagnose, and resolve network communication problems by consolidating all pertinent error messages into a dedicated stream.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.19.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core 0.19.0 includes improvements to network performance, transaction policy, and wallet functionality. This release enhances block propagation, provides new controls for transaction fee rates, and strengthens network privacy defaults. Various RPC calls and internal processes have also been optimized for better performance and reduced resource usage.
highlights: **P2P:** Introduced two dedicated outbound block-relay-only connections to improve block propagation speed and reliability.
**Policy:** Updated transaction relay policy to consider transactions sending to future native witness outputs as standard.
**P2P Privacy:** Disabled bloom filtering by default.

**Wallet & RPC:** Added a GUI option to create new wallets, made Bech32 addresses the default for new address generation, and introduced an optional `maxfeerate` parameter to the `sendrawtransaction` RPC.
**Node Performance:** Optimized `getrawmempool` and `getblockstats` RPC commands for faster execution, and reduced overall memory usage by 9%.

This PR updates the `CChainParams` or related structures to mark these old deployments (like SegWit) as `BURIED`. This stops the node from constantly checking and evaluating their state transitions, simplifying the consensus code path and reducing unnecessary computations for already-activated features.

prs.technical_summary: Bloom filters, a probabilistic data structure, were historically used by lightweight clients (SPV) to query for relevant transactions without downloading the entire blockchain. However, they have known privacy drawbacks due to fingerprinting and can impose a resource burden on full nodes. This change modifies the default node configuration to no longer advertise or enable bloom filtering support upon establishing new peer connections. While the functionality might remain accessible via explicit configuration flags or specific peer requests, its default disablement promotes the transition towards superior privacy-preserving alternatives like BIP 157/158 Compact Block Filters for wallet synchronization.

prs.public_summary: This PR removes an unused and potentially problematic user agent string field (`strSubVer`) from the `CNode` object. By removing unused code, it reduces memory footprint and potential attack vectors, contributing to a leaner and more secure codebase.
prs.technical_summary: The change entails removing the `CNode::strSubVer` member variable, which was previously intended for storing a node's sub-version string but was found to be unused in practice. This also involves removing any associated initialization, assignment, or access points for this member. The primary benefit is reducing the memory footprint of `CNode` objects and eliminating a field that, if ever mistakenly used without proper sanitization, could pose a security risk by storing unsanitized user-controlled data.

prs.description: Make whitebind/whitelist permissions more flexible
prs.author: NicolasDorier
prs.public_summary: This PR significantly enhances the flexibility of `whitebind` and `whitelist` peer permissions, allowing node operators to fine-tune what trusted peers can do. This provides more granular control over network interactions and security policies.
prs.technical_summary: This PR introduces a new permission bitmask system for `whitebind` and `whitelist` connections, replacing the previous boolean approach. It modifies the `CNode` class to store specific permissions such as `PF_RELAY`, `PF_MEMPOOL`, `PF_RESERVE`, and `PF_DOWNLOAD`. The network processing logic in `src/net_processing.cpp` and `src/net.cpp` is updated to check these new flags before allowing actions like transaction relay, mempool access, or block downloading, enabling much more granular control over trusted peer behavior and greatly increasing configuration flexibility.

prs.description: [Fix] Allow connection of a noban banned peer
prs.author: NicolasDorier
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes an issue that incorrectly prevented peers with the `noban` permission from connecting, even when they were temporarily banned. It ensures that designated trusted peers can always establish a connection, regardless of transient network or behavioral issues.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the peer connection establishment logic to correctly prioritize the `noban` permission. Specifically, it adjusts the ban enforcement mechanism in `src/net.cpp` or `src/net_processing.cpp` to check for the `PF_NOBAN` flag *before* applying any ban status. This ensures that if a peer has the `noban` permission, ban checks are explicitly bypassed, allowing the connection to proceed even if its IP address is listed in the ban map, thereby honoring the intended `noban` behavior.

prs.description: Add ChaCha20Poly1305@Bitcoin AEAD
prs.author: jonasschnelli
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces support for the ChaCha20-Poly1305 Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) cipher suite. This enhances the cryptographic options available for secure communication within Bitcoin Core, offering a modern and robust alternative.
prs.technical_summary: This PR integrates the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD construction into Bitcoin Core's cryptographic primitives library. This involves implementing the necessary functions for encryption, decryption, authentication tag generation, and verification, conforming to the `AEAD` interface. The addition provides a new secure cryptographic option, potentially for use in future secure transport layers (like v2 P2P encrypted connections) or other areas requiring strong authenticated encryption, offering improved performance and security characteristics over some older ciphers.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.18.2.
release_summary: This release primarily focuses on improvements to wallet functionality, including bug fixes related to transaction creation and enhancements for Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions. It also includes important updates to the build system's security and quality checks.
highlights: **Wallet:** Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions (PSBTs) now shuffle inputs and outputs after joining, enhancing privacy during collaboration.
**Wallet:** The `walletcreatefundedpsbt` RPC call now automatically utilizes the wallet's configured default Replace-by-Fee (RBF) setting.
**Wallet:** A bug was fixed that prevented the correct application of the user-defined `-maxtxfee` limit during transaction creation.
**Build System:** Issues with argument passing in the `check-symbols` and `check-security` build scripts were resolved, ensuring correct execution of code quality and security checks.

prs.description: [0.18] net: Log to net category for exceptions in ProcessMessages
prs.author: instagibbs
prs.public_summary: This PR improves logging for network-related errors, specifically by routing exceptions in `ProcessMessages` to the `net` category. This makes it easier for users and developers to diagnose and troubleshoot network connectivity and message processing issues.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the exception handling within the `ProcessMessages` function, which is responsible for deserializing and processing incoming network messages from peers. Exceptions caught during this critical process are now explicitly logged under the `LogCategory::NET` category. This targeted logging enables more granular filtering and analysis of network-specific errors, greatly assisting in debugging peer-to-peer communication failures and message validation issues.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.18.1.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core 0.18.1 focuses on enhancing wallet reliability, RPC consistency, and network robustness. This release strengthens transaction fee limit enforcement, standardizes address generation for multisignature scripts, and refines error reporting for unspendable funds. Additionally, stability improvements have been made to Tor integration.
highlights: **RPC/Network Robustness:** Stricter encoding rules are enforced for non-witness transactions, preventing non-standard encodings to improve network robustness.
**Wallet:** Consistent address generation for multisignature scripts utilizing uncompressed public keys is now mandated to always produce a legacy (P2SH) address.
**Wallet:** The `-maxtxfee` limit is more strictly enforced, with transaction funding operations now aborting if they exceed the configured maximum fee.
**Wallet/RPC:** Enhanced error reporting is provided when the wallet encounters transactions missing crucial redeem or witness scripts, improving diagnostic clarity for unspendable funds.
**P2P:** Tor integration stability is improved by ensuring the Tor event loop is correctly shut down, particularly during application exit.

prs.description: p2p: Avoid logging transaction decode errors to stderr
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR reduces log spam by preventing common transaction decode errors from being outputted to standard error (stderr) in the P2P layer. This makes logs cleaner and more focused on critical issues, improving debuggability.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, malformed or invalid transactions received over the P2P network often generated excessive decode error messages on `stderr`. This change modifies the transaction deserialization or validation routines within the P2P networking code, likely within `src/net.cpp`. It suppresses these specific non-critical errors from being logged at high verbosity levels or redirects them to a more appropriate debug-only channel, significantly reducing noise in standard output for non-critical P2P events.

prs.description: 0.18: fix: tor: Call event_base_loopbreak from the event's callback
prs.author: promag
prs.public_summary: Fixes a bug in the Tor integration that ensures the Tor event loop is correctly shut down. This improves the stability and reliability of Tor connections, especially during application exit.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses a bug in the Tor event handling by ensuring `event_base_loopbreak()` is called from within the appropriate event's callback function. Previously, this might have been called in a context where it would not correctly signal the `libevent` loop to exit. Moving the call into the callback guarantees the event loop termination is properly processed asynchronously, preventing potential hangs or improper shutdown of the Tor thread.

prs.description: fix: tor: Call event_base_loopbreak from the event's callback
prs.author: promag
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug in the Tor control logic, ensuring that the event loop is correctly broken from within an event's callback. This improves the reliability and shutdown behavior of Tor connections in Bitcoin Core.
prs.technical_summary: The Tor control connection relies on `libevent` for asynchronous event handling. When shutting down the Tor thread or handling specific events that require loop termination, it's crucial to break out of the `event_base_dispatch` loop. Previously, the call to `event_base_loopbreak()` might have been made from a context outside the `libevent` event's callback, which could lead to race conditions or incorrect behavior. This fix ensures that `event_base_loopbreak()` is invoked directly from within the event's callback function, guaranteeing proper signal handling and thread termination logic within the `libevent` framework.

prs.description: net: Make poll in InterruptibleRecv only filter for POLLIN events.
prs.author: tecnovert
prs.public_summary: Improves network efficiency by ensuring the `InterruptibleRecv` function only waits for incoming data. This makes network communication more focused and potentially more performant by avoiding unnecessary checks.
prs.technical_summary: This PR refines the `poll` system call within the `InterruptibleRecv` function to exclusively monitor for `POLLIN` events. Previously, it might have been configured to check for other event types, leading to spurious wakeups. By explicitly filtering for `POLLIN`, the function now wakes up only when data is actually available to be read, reducing CPU cycles spent on context switching and processing irrelevant events, thereby optimizing network receive operations.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.18.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core 0.18.0 introduces a new command-line tool for offline wallet management and significant enhancements to descriptor support and Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions. The release improves P2P network performance, security, and communication through better random number generation, memory optimizations, and refined ban management. Additionally, the build system now supports RISC-V, and RPC and configuration options have been updated for improved functionality and robustness.
highlights: **Wallet:** A new command-line utility, `bitcoin-wallet`, is introduced for creating and managing wallets offline, alongside enhanced descriptor support for key origin data and checksums.
**P2P Network:** Network performance and security are improved through better random number generation, memory optimizations, refined ban management, and the default enabling of 'reject' messages.

**RPC & Mining:** New RPC commands for Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions (PSBTs) and `submitheader` are added, with a critical fix for PSBT fee calculation, and `getblocktemplate` calls now require explicit SegWit rule specification.

**Configuration & Build System:** Build support for the RISC-V architecture is introduced, the minimum supported Windows version is set to Windows 7, and configuration parsing now warns about unrecognized sections while explicitly preventing '#' in `rpcpassword`.

prs.description: net: Add missing locking annotation for vNodes. vNodes is guarded by cs_vNodes.
prs.author: practicalswift
prs.public_summary: This PR adds critical locking annotations for the `vNodes` vector, explicitly stating that it is guarded by `cs_vNodes`. This improves code readability and helps static analysis tools identify potential concurrency issues, enhancing the overall safety and maintainability of the networking code.
prs.technical_summary: This change primarily involves adding `LOCKS_EXCLUDED()` or similar annotations (e.g., `GUARDED_BY(cs_vNodes)`) to member variables or functions accessing the `vNodes` vector within the networking subsystem. This provides crucial information to static analysis tools, allowing them to verify correct mutex usage (`cs_vNodes`) when `vNodes` is accessed or modified. While not a runtime behavioral change, it significantly aids in preventing future race conditions and ensures thread safety guarantees are explicitly documented and checked.

prs.description: net: Correct comparison of addr count
prs.author: dongcarl
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a subtle bug in the networking code related to comparing network address counts. Correcting this ensures more accurate peer management and network address handling within Bitcoin Core.
prs.technical_summary: The PR addresses an issue where an incorrect comparison operator or logic was used when evaluating the number of network addresses. This fix likely resides in the `src/net/` directory, specifically within the code responsible for tracking and managing known peer addresses (e.g., `CAddrMan`). Correcting this ensures the address manager behaves as expected, preventing potential edge-case issues with peer discovery or address propagation.

prs.description: Select orphan transaction uniformly for eviction
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR modifies how orphan transactions are evicted from the mempool, ensuring they are selected uniformly rather than in a potentially biased manner. This improvement makes the eviction process fairer and more robust, preventing certain transactions from being unfairly prioritized or perpetually stuck.
prs.technical_summary: This commit alters the orphan transaction eviction strategy within the mempool. Instead of a deterministic or arrival-order-based eviction, it introduces a mechanism to randomly or uniformly select an orphan transaction for removal when the orphan pool size exceeds its limit. This likely involves using a random number generator to pick an index or iterator from the `mapOrphanTransactions` structure, thereby distributing the eviction pressure more evenly across the set of orphaned transactions.

prs.description: Drop IsLimited in favor of IsReachable
prs.author: Empact
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors network address reachability logic by replacing `IsLimited` with the more comprehensive `IsReachable`. This simplifies the network code, makes address handling more consistent, and provides a clearer understanding of which network interfaces are genuinely capable of outward connections.
prs.technical_summary: This change involves migrating the usage of the `IsLimited()` method, which likely checked for specific 'limited' network types (e.g., non-routable, loopback), to the more general `IsReachable()` method for determining address connectivity. This likely entails modifying existing call sites within the network logic (e.g., peer discovery, connection management) to invoke `IsReachable()` and potentially updating its implementation to consolidate various reachability checks. The goal is to streamline the network address evaluation logic and reduce code duplication.

prs.description: BIP 158: Compact Block Filters for Light Clients
prs.author: jimpo
prs.public_summary: This PR introduces BIP 158 support, enabling compact block filters for light clients in Bitcoin Core. This significantly improves privacy and efficiency for lightweight wallets by allowing them to sync and verify transactions without downloading entire blocks.
prs.technical_summary: This significant PR implements the full specification for BIP 158, "Compact Block Filters for Light Clients." It involves creating and maintaining new data structures for `cfilter` and `cfilterheader` objects, which are small cryptographic commitments to the transactions within a block. Full nodes now generate these filters for each block, making them available for light clients to request and download. This allows light clients to efficiently determine if a block contains transactions relevant to their wallets, drastically reducing bandwidth requirements and enhancing privacy by avoiding specific address queries to full nodes.

prs.description: P2P: Make peer timeout configurable, speed up very slow test and ensure correct code path tested.
prs.author: zallarak
prs.public_summary: This PR makes the P2P peer connection timeout configurable, allowing for more adaptable network behavior. It also significantly speeds up a previously very slow test by ensuring more efficient and targeted validation of network logic.
prs.technical_summary: The P2P peer timeout, previously a hardcoded value, is now exposed as a configurable option (e.g., via `bitcoin.conf` or command-line arguments), modifying the relevant `CNode` or `NetGroupManager` logic. Concurrently, a particularly slow network-related test, likely involving peer timeouts, was optimized. This optimization involved refactoring the test to directly trigger and assert against the specific code paths under examination rather than relying on lengthy real-time waits, drastically reducing execution time while still thoroughly validating the timeout mechanism.

prs.description: Never bind INADDR_ANY by default, and warn when doing so explicitly
prs.author: luke-jr
prs.public_summary: This PR changes the default network binding behavior to never use `INADDR_ANY` automatically and issues a warning if it's explicitly configured. This enhances security by preventing the node from inadvertently listening on all available network interfaces, reducing exposure to untrusted networks.
prs.technical_summary: This change modifies the network binding logic to disallow `INADDR_ANY` (0.0.0.0) as the default listen address. Instead, the node will now bind to specific, typically localhost or configured, interfaces by default, which may involve iterating through local network interfaces to select an appropriate one. Furthermore, if `INADDR_ANY` is explicitly configured by the user, a warning will be logged to inform them of the broader network exposure, ensuring users are aware of the security implications.

prs.description: Skip stale tip checking if outbound connections are off or if reindexing.
prs.author: gmaxwell
prs.public_summary: This PR optimizes node behavior by skipping the stale tip checking mechanism when outbound connections are disabled or the node is reindexing. This prevents unnecessary resource consumption and log spam in specific operational modes, improving efficiency during startup and maintenance.
prs.technical_summary: This commit introduces conditional logic to bypass the `CheckForStaleTip()` function (or similar logic that checks for a stale chain tip) when specific conditions are met. Specifically, it adds checks to see if outbound connections are globally disabled (`-connect=0` or similar configuration) or if the node is currently in a reindexing state (`fReindex`). By short-circuiting this check under these conditions, it avoids redundant network requests and processing, streamlining node operation during non-standard or setup phases.

prs.description: net: Allow connections from misbehavior banned peers
prs.author: gmaxwell
prs.public_summary: This PR adjusts how Bitcoin Core handles network bans, potentially allowing manually specified or trusted peers to connect even if their IP address has previously been associated with misbehavior. This could improve network reachability and flexibility for specific node operators.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the networking subsystem's ban management logic to allow connection attempts from peers whose IP addresses are currently on the misbehavior ban list under specific conditions. This typically applies to explicitly added `addnode` peers or those manually connected via RPC, allowing them to bypass the initial ban check for connection establishment. The goal is to provide operators with a mechanism to override blanket IP bans for known or critical peers, facilitating re-evaluation of their behavior without manual ban list clearance.

prs.description: p2p: Do not relay banned IP addresses
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the P2P network security and efficiency by preventing the node from advertising or relaying network addresses of known banned peers. This helps to isolate misbehaving nodes and reduces wasted network resources.
prs.technical_summary: This change modifies the P2P address management and relay logic. When an `addr` message is constructed or forwarded, the node will now filter out any IP addresses that are currently marked as banned within its internal `CAddrMan` or equivalent data structure. This prevents broadcasting addresses of unproductive or malicious peers to other nodes, thereby improving the overall health and resilience of the network by limiting the propagation of undesirable peer information.

prs.description: 0.18: [p2p] Enable reject messages by default
prs.author: jnewbery
prs.public_summary: This PR, targeting the 0.18 release, enables "reject" messages by default on the P2P network, providing clearer communication when a peer sends an invalid transaction or block. This helps nodes quickly identify and troubleshoot issues with other peers.
prs.technical_summary: This PR changes a default configuration setting. Previously, `reject` messages (P2P messages indicating that a transaction or block was rejected for a specific reason) might have been disabled or opt-in. This change modifies the default node behavior to send `reject` messages whenever an invalid transaction, block, or other protocol message is received. This is achieved by updating a boolean flag, likely `fSendReject` or similar, within the `CNode` or `NetGroup` logic to `true` by default, improving debugging and peer-to-peer fault isolation.

The reversion restores the deterministic or non-randomized method of fetching block and transaction data from peers, implying the randomization introduced unforeseen issues, such as performance overhead or unintended privacy consequences, justifying a rollback for the stable release.

prs.description: [Net] Switch nPrevNodeCount to vNodesSize
prs.author: pstratem
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors internal network node counting in Bitcoin Core for better maintainability and clarity. It switches an internal variable from `nPrevNodeCount` to `vNodesSize`, reflecting the underlying data structure more accurately.
prs.technical_summary: The change updates an internal counter in the P2P networking subsystem, which tracks the number of currently connected peers. Instead of `nPrevNodeCount`, which might imply a historical or previous state, the variable now directly uses `vNodesSize`, a more immediate and accurate representation derived from the size of the `vNodes` vector that holds peer connections. This code cleanup improves readability, reduces potential for off-by-one errors, and ensures the counter precisely reflects the real-time number of active peer connections.

prs.description: p2p: Remove dead code for nVersion=10300
prs.author: MarcoFalke
prs.public_summary: This PR cleans up the Bitcoin Core codebase by removing obsolete peer-to-peer networking code. It specifically targets logic related to a very old protocol version, improving maintainability and reducing code footprint.
prs.technical_summary: Protocol version `nVersion=10300` corresponds to Bitcoin Core 0.3.x, which is no longer active or supported on the network. This PR identifies and removes `if (nVersion >= 10300)` checks and their associated code blocks, which previously handled features or behaviors specific to this ancient protocol version. The removal eliminates dead code, simplifying the P2P codebase and making it easier for developers to reason about the current protocol implementation without the burden of legacy compatibility checks, thereby improving overall code quality.

prs.description: net: implement poll
prs.author: pstratem
prs.public_summary: This PR integrates the `poll()` system call for event handling in the networking layer, replacing or augmenting older mechanisms. This can lead to more efficient handling of multiple network connections, potentially improving network throughput and reducing CPU usage.
prs.technical_summary: This commit introduces the `poll()` system call for multiplexing I/O operations across multiple network sockets. This likely involves refactoring the existing socket event loop, possibly replacing `select()` or a similar older mechanism with `poll()`. The implementation would involve creating a `pollfd` array, registering file descriptors for network sockets, and iterating over the returned events to handle incoming data or outgoing buffer readiness, leading to a more scalable and efficient event processing model.

prs.description: blockfilter: Avoid out-of-bounds script access.
prs.author: jimpo
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical security vulnerability in Bitcoin Core's block filter implementation. It prevents potential crashes or exploits caused by out-of-bounds memory access when processing malformed scripts within compact block filters.
prs.technical_summary: The vulnerability resided within the block filter processing code, specifically during the handling of transaction scripts for compact block filters (BIP 158). A maliciously crafted script could lead to an attempt to access memory outside of its allocated buffer, potentially causing a crash or enabling an exploit. The fix introduces robust bounds checking and validation mechanisms to ensure all script accesses remain strictly within their designated memory regions. This enhances the security and stability of the filter subsystem by preventing out-of-bounds errors.

prs.description: [net] add dnsseed.emzy.de to DNS seeds
prs.author: Emzy
prs.public_summary: This PR adds a new DNS seed, `dnsseed.emzy.de`, to the list of default DNS seeds used by Bitcoin Core. Expanding the list of trusted DNS seeds helps new nodes discover peers more reliably and quickly, improving network decentralization and initial bootstrapping.
prs.technical_summary: This commit directly modifies the `src/chainparams.cpp` or a similar configuration file to append `dnsseed.emzy.de` to the array or vector of hardcoded DNS seed hostnames. This new entry will be used by nodes during initial bootstrapping to query for a list of active Bitcoin nodes, thereby expanding the available pool of initial peer discovery points and enhancing network robustness against individual seed failures.

prs.description: randomize GETDATA(tx) request order and introduce bias toward outbound
prs.author: naumenkogs
prs.public_summary: This PR improves network privacy and efficiency by randomizing the order of transaction requests and biasing requests towards outbound peers. This makes transaction origin harder to trace and optimizes transaction propagation.
prs.technical_summary: The changes affect the peer-to-peer networking layer's `GETDATA` message construction. First, the order of transaction hashes within `GETDATA(tx)` requests sent to peers is now randomized, obfuscating the original order in which transactions were seen or requested. Second, a probabilistic preference is introduced to send `GETDATA` requests to outbound connections (peers initiated by this node), potentially improving relay reliability. These modifications are implemented within `net_processing.cpp` or `p2p.cpp` to modify how `CNode` objects generate and prioritize requests.

prs.description: Return of the Banman
prs.author: dongcarl
prs.public_summary: This PR reintroduces or significantly improves the 'Banman' component, enhancing Bitcoin Core's ability to manage and apply network bans for misbehaving peers. This helps protect the node from malicious or poorly configured connections.
prs.technical_summary: This PR re-establishes or significantly refactors a dedicated `Banman` component within the networking subsystem, centralizing the management of peer bans. This involves encapsulating the logic for adding, removing, persisting, and querying banned IP addresses or peers into a well-defined class. The refactor aims to improve the robustness and consistency of ban management, simplifying interactions with the peer-to-peer network logic and leading to more effective handling of misbehaving nodes.

prs.description: Make orphan processing interruptible
prs.author: sipa
prs.public_summary: This PR improves the responsiveness and resource management of the Bitcoin Core node by allowing the complex process of handling orphaned blocks to be interrupted. This prevents the node from getting stuck in long computations during shutdown or reorgs, leading to a smoother user experience.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, the `ProcessNewBlock` function, specifically when handling orphan blocks, could block threads indefinitely. This change introduces an interrupt mechanism by passing an `InterruptBlock` signal to the `ProcessOrphanBlock` function, allowing the block processing thread to be gracefully halted. This is achieved by checking the interrupt signal within the processing loop, ensuring that `BlockManager` operations can be terminated cleanly, particularly during node shutdown or when a chain reorg occurs.

prs.description: [addrman, net] Ensure tried collisions resolve, and allow feeler connections to existing outbound netgroups
prs.author: sdaftuar
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances Bitcoin Core's peer discovery and network health by improving how it manages known addresses and allowing more robust connection attempts. It helps nodes find and connect to diverse peers more efficiently.
prs.technical_summary: This change modifies the `CAddrMan` behavior to ensure that address collisions in the tried table are properly resolved, preventing potential issues with address management. Additionally, it updates the peer-to-peer networking logic to permit feeler connections to target netgroups where existing outbound connections already exist, thereby improving the diversity and reliability of peer discovery by exploring more potential connections.

prs.description: Report minfeefilter value in getpeerinfo rpc
prs.author: ajtowns
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances the `getpeerinfo` RPC command by adding the `minfeefilter` value. Users can now easily see the minimum fee rate a connected peer will relay, improving insights into network fee policy propagation.
prs.technical_summary: The `minfeefilter` value represents the lowest transaction fee rate (in satoshis per virtual byte) that a peer will accept for relaying new transactions. This PR modifies the `getpeerinfo` RPC handler to include this specific attribute in its JSON output for each connected peer. The implementation involves accessing the stored `minfeefilter` property from each `CNode` object and serializing it into the RPC response. This provides node operators with more granular information about the transaction relay policies of their peer connections.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.17.2.

**P2P:** Support for the ChaCha20-Poly1305 Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data (AEAD) cipher suite was added to enhance secure communication.
**P2P:** Network event handling was improved with the integration of the `poll()` system call, potentially leading to more efficient management of multiple network connections.
**P2P:** Transaction relay bugs were resolved, and a mechanism was introduced to expire in-flight transactions from peer maps, improving propagation reliability.
**RPC:** The RPC interface was modified to prevent the creation of non-standard raw transactions, aligning with network relay policies for improved transaction reliability.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.17.1.
release_summary: This minor version release of Bitcoin Core 0.17.1 primarily focuses on stability, security, and wallet functionality. It incorporates several bug fixes for transaction creation and wallet management, alongside security enhancements for network binding and wallet signing. Key improvements also extend to the Partially Signed Bitcoin Transaction (PSBT) interface and various RPC commands.
highlights: **P2P:** Enhanced network security by preventing nodes from binding to `INADDR_ANY` by default and issuing a warning when explicitly configured.

prs.description: fix a deserialization overflow edge case
prs.author: kazcw
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a critical edge case where specific malformed data could cause a deserialization overflow, improving the robustness and security of Bitcoin Core. It prevents potential crashes or denial-of-service vulnerabilities when processing network messages or blockchain data.
prs.technical_summary: The fix addresses a specific deserialization vulnerability where an attacker-crafted message or data structure could cause an integer overflow during deserialization. This typically involves adding explicit bounds checking or using safer integer types/operations (e.g., `size_t` for sizes, `checked_add`, `checked_mul`) when reading variable-length data, counts, or offsets from the network stream or disk. By preventing the overflow, the PR mitigates potential denial-of-service attacks, memory corruption, or other undefined behavior that could arise from incorrect size calculations or buffer allocations during data reconstruction.

prs.description: fix uninitialized read when stringifying an addrLocal
prs.author: kazcw
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes a bug where an uninitialized variable could be read when converting a local network address to a string. This resolves a potential source of undefined behavior or crashes, making the node more stable and reliable.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.17.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core 0.17.0 introduces significant advancements in wallet management, including dynamic wallet creation and loading via RPC, and a new 'label' API that supersedes the legacy 'account' system. The release enhances network security and node stability through critical bug fixes, such as addressing crashes from duplicate transaction inputs, and by implementing protections against denial-of-service attacks. Further improvements include optimized resource utilization during block synchronization and streamlined build processes with updated dependencies.
highlights: **Wallet:** The `createwallet` and `loadwallet` RPCs were introduced, enabling dynamic creation and loading of wallets at runtime, while a new 'label' API replaces the deprecated 'account' system.
**Consensus/Network:** A crash bug triggered by transactions with duplicate inputs was resolved, and a maximum size for block locators was introduced to mitigate potential denial-of-service attacks.

**Wallet/RPC:** The `scantxoutset` RPC method was added to efficiently scan the UTXO set using output descriptors, and the `createwallet` RPC gained a `disableprivatekeys` option for watch-only wallets.
**Performance/Privacy:** The block loading thread's priority was lowered to reduce CPU resource consumption, and wallet privacy was improved by shuffling coins before grouping for transactions.
**Build System:** Support for Qt4 and Python 2 was removed, streamlining the codebase, and the minimum macOS version requirement for releases was raised to 10.10+.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.16.1.
release_summary: This minor release of Bitcoin Core version 0.16.1 focuses on improving network stability, security, and node performance. Key updates include refined transaction standardness rules and critical fixes for concurrency issues within block validation. Additionally, the release enhances peer-to-peer network resilience and extends build system compatibility to support a wider range of hardware.
highlights: **Policy:** Introduced or refined several transaction standardness rules to improve network efficiency and security.
**Validation:** Resolved concurrency issues in the `ActivateBestChain()` function, ensuring more reliable blockchain updates and preventing invalid chain states.
**P2P:** Implemented a limit on the number of IP addresses learned from each DNS seeder to enhance network resilience and diversity.
**Wallet:** Fixed an issue where the `zapwallettxes` RPC command did not correctly interact with multiwallet setups, preventing data corruption.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.16.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core 0.16.0 introduces comprehensive Segregated Witness (SegWit) support within the wallet, including native Bech32 address generation and usage, and sets Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) wallets as the default for new installations. The release also includes significant performance enhancements through default SHA256 assembly optimizations and an improved mempool sorting algorithm. Additionally, various RPC methods were updated or deprecated for a more modular interface, alongside general stability and build system improvements.
highlights: **Wallet:** Full Segregated Witness (SegWit) support is now integrated into the wallet and user interfaces, including the ability to generate and use native Bech32 addresses.
**Wallet:** New wallets are created as Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) by default; wallets created with version 0.16.0 are not compatible with previous versions.
**Performance:** SHA256 hashing optimizations for architectures supporting SSE4 are now enabled by default, significantly speeding up synchronization and block validation.
**Mempool:** Transaction prioritization is improved by sorting the mempool based on the minimum of a transaction's own feerate and its ancestor's feerate.
**P2P:** Support for signalling NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED (BIP159) by pruned nodes is included, allowing them to indicate their limited block-serving capability.

prs.description: net: Split socket create/connect
prs.author: theuni
prs.public_summary: This PR refactors the network code by separating the creation of a socket from its connection process, improving the modularity and maintainability of the networking stack. This makes future network improvements and error handling more straightforward.
prs.technical_summary: Architecturally, this PR refactors the `net` module by decoupling the `socket()` system call from `connect()`. Previously, these operations might have been combined or tightly coupled within a single function. Now, a socket can be created, configured (e.g., set non-blocking, apply socket options), and then later explicitly connected, allowing for more granular control over the socket's lifecycle. This change primarily affects `src/net.cpp` and related network connection functions, introducing new helper functions or modifying existing ones to reflect this separation.

prs.description: net: Add missing locks in net.{cpp,h}
prs.author: practicalswift
prs.public_summary: This PR fixes potential concurrency issues in the networking code by adding missing locks, improving the stability and reliability of Bitcoin Core. It ensures thread-safe access to shared network resources, preventing crashes and undefined behavior.
prs.technical_summary: This PR addresses thread safety concerns within the `net` component by identifying and adding `LOCK()` or `RecursiveLock()` guards around access to shared data structures or critical sections in `src/net.cpp` and `src/net.h`. This prevents race conditions that could occur when multiple threads concurrently modify or read network state, such as peer lists or connection information. The changes are localized to specific functions and data members that were identified as lacking proper synchronization mechanisms, thus ensuring data consistency in a multi-threaded environment.

prs.description: Use GetDesireableServiceFlags in seeds, dnsseeds, fixing static seed adding
prs.author: TheBlueMatt
prs.public_summary: This PR improves how Bitcoin Core connects to initial peers by ensuring it actively seeks out nodes offering useful services, such as full blockchain data, when using seed nodes. This helps new nodes connect to high-quality peers more reliably and efficiently, improving network bootstrapping.
prs.technical_summary: Previously, the logic for selecting peers from hardcoded seeds and DNS seeds might not have consistently filtered for nodes providing specific 'desirable' services, such as `NODE_NETWORK` (full blockchain data). This PR integrates the `GetDesireableServiceFlags` function into the seed processing logic. This ensures that when new peers are discovered via seeds, they are checked against a configured set of required service flags, preventing connections to 'light' nodes or those not offering the necessary services for a full node. This fixes potential issues where statically added seeds might not have correctly applied service flag filtering, leading to suboptimal peer connections.

prs.description: Update chainTxData for 0.16

This PR updates these values, which typically include a recent block hash and total chain work. By providing more up-to-date data for the 0.16 release, new nodes can bootstrap more quickly by assuming validity of blocks up to this point, significantly reducing initial sync and validation time.

prs.description: Add vConnect to CConnman::Options

A new member, `vConnect`, is added, which is a vector of network addresses (likely `CNetAddr` or `CService`). This allows explicit, granular control over a list of addresses that `CConnman` should attempt to connect to, extending beyond the default DNS seeding or hardcoded addnode mechanisms.

prs.description: script: Change SignatureHash input index check to an assert.

This PR replaces that condition with an `assert()`. This change indicates that reaching an invalid input index at this stage is considered an unrecoverable programming error, as prior validation should have prevented it. This provides clearer error signaling for developers, causing immediate failure in debug builds if this invariant is violated.

prs.description: Do not send (potentially) invalid headers in response to getheaders
prs.author: TheBlueMatt
prs.public_summary: This PR prevents Bitcoin Core from sending potentially invalid block headers to other nodes in response to `getheaders` requests. This improves network integrity by ensuring that nodes only propagate valid chain information, protecting against misbehavior and chain splits.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the logic for handling `getheaders` requests in `src/net_processing.cpp`. It ensures that only headers which are known to be valid and part of the node's best-known chain (or a valid fork) are included in the response. This likely involves additional checks on the headers retrieved from the block index before they are serialized and sent. The goal is to prevent the dissemination of orphaned or otherwise invalid headers, which could mislead other peers and degrade network health.

prs.description: [net] Ignore getheaders requests for very old side blocks
prs.author: jimpo

If a request targets a block whose height is significantly older than the current tip and is not on the main chain, the request is now silently ignored. This avoids expensive database lookups and processing for side branches that are extremely unlikely to ever become the best chain, thereby conserving node resources.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.15.1.
release_summary: This release primarily focuses on enhancing network robustness and security against invalid or stale chain data, alongside improvements to wallet stability and mining configuration. Key updates include refined peer management to ensure nodes connect to healthy chains, preventing issues from misconfigured mining options, and safeguarding wallet data integrity.
highlights: **P2P/Security:** Enhanced network robustness by improving peer disconnection logic for nodes providing invalid or stale chain data, and by tracking invalid blocks more efficiently to prevent building on incorrect chains.
**Mining/RPC:** Clarified and corrected `blockmaxsize` and `blockmaxweight` configuration options, preventing accidental transaction loss for miners and deprecating direct block size limiting.
**Wallet:** Implemented a safeguard to prevent potential data corruption by disallowing the simultaneous opening of multiple copies of the same wallet database.
**RPC/Debug:** Introduced a hidden debug argument, `-minimumchainwork`, allowing advanced users to specify a custom minimum work value for chain validation.
**RPC/Security:** Strengthened RPC command security by preventing `dumpwallet` from overwriting existing files and making `listsinceblock` error on unknown block hashes.

prs.description: Connect to a new outbound peer if our tip is stale
prs.author: sdaftuar
prs.public_summary: This PR enhances network connectivity by prompting Bitcoin Core to establish a new outbound connection if its blockchain tip becomes outdated. This helps nodes stay better synchronized with the network, improving decentralization and resistance to partition attacks.
prs.technical_summary: This PR implements logic within the peer-to-peer networking layer to monitor the recency of the local blockchain tip. If the tip is detected as 'stale' (i.e., significantly behind the network's consensus), the node will proactively attempt to establish a new outbound connection to a different peer. This mechanism aims to break out of potentially bad peer connections or network partitions by seeking fresh connections, thereby improving block propagation and overall network synchronization.

prs.description: net processing: swap out signals for an interface class
prs.author: theuni
prs.public_summary: This refactoring improves the modularity and testability of Bitcoin Core's network processing logic by replacing a signal-slot system with a more explicit interface. It enhances code organization and makes it easier to develop and test network-related components independently.
prs.technical_summary: This PR replaces the use of global Boost.Signals2 with a dependency injection pattern utilizing an interface class for network processing components. Instead of broadcasting events via signals, an abstract interface now defines methods for communication between these components. Concrete implementations of this interface can be passed into network processing objects, allowing for easier mocking in tests and clearer explicit dependencies.

prs.description: Disconnect from outbound peers with bad headers chains
prs.author: sdaftuar
prs.public_summary: This PR improves network hygiene by ensuring Bitcoin Core disconnects from outbound peers that provide bad or invalid blockchain headers. This helps the node maintain a robust and secure view of the network by rejecting peers attempting to propagate incorrect chain information.
prs.technical_summary: This PR modifies the peer management logic specifically concerning header validation for outbound connections. It likely involves tracking the validity of header chains received from outbound peers and, upon detection of consistently invalid header sequences, initiating a disconnection. This mechanism helps to quickly identify and remove peers that are misbehaving or propagating erroneous chain data, thereby improving the quality of network connections.

prs.description: [P2P] When clearing addrman clear mapInfo and mapAddr.

This ensures that all internal maps and indices used by the address manager are properly synchronized and emptied, preventing stale data and potential issues when `addrman` is re-initialized or cleared.

This allows custom chain forks or testnets to be deployed and synchronized more rapidly without requiring a full recompile or extensive initial block download, facilitating development and specialized network operations.

summary: Release notes and changes for Bitcoin Core 0.15.0.
release_summary: Bitcoin Core version 0.15.0 introduces initial support for managing multiple independent wallets from a single node instance. This release also features significant performance improvements, particularly in transaction processing and cryptographic hashing, and refines transaction fee estimation for greater accuracy and user control. Further enhancements include improved wallet privacy mechanisms and the removal of coin age-based transaction priority.
highlights: **Wallet:** Implemented initial support for managing multiple independent wallets from a single Bitcoin Core instance.
**Transaction Policy:** Removed transaction priority based on coin age and free transaction relay from mempool and relay policies.
**Performance:** Integrated SSE4 optimized SHA256 hashing and improved mempool efficiency for distinguishing transaction types.
**Fee Estimation:** Enhanced transaction fee estimation logic, providing more accurate predictions and extended control options via RPCs and the GUI.
**Wallet Privacy:** Introduced the use of a distinct internal Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) key chain for change outputs and ensured keypool indexes are never reused.
